author: jon-bell
body:
## Summary Fixes [issue #427](https://github.com/pawtograder/platform/issues/427): **Create GitHub Repositories** on the instructor **Test Assignment** page did nothing for assignments with `group_config === "groups"` when the instructor was not in a student assignment group (e.g. after the group formation deadline). ## Root cause - **Group repos** are only created in the `assignment_groups_members` branch of `autograder-create-repos-for-student`. - **Individual repos** were explicitly excluded when `group_config === "groups"`. - Instructors testing the assignment often have no group membership row, so neither path ran; the UI still showed success because failures were only appended to the response message. ## Solution - Optional body field `for_test_assignment` with `assignment_id`, passed only from the Test Assignment UI via `CreateStudentReposButton` (`forTestAssignment` prop) and `autograderCreateReposForStudent(..., { forTestAssignment: true })` — not implied by every `assignmentId` call. - Edge function: if `for_test_assignment` is set, require `assignment_id`; for JWT callers, verify the user is **instructor or grader** for that assignment’s class (or **platform admin**) before allowing the groups-only bypass. Internal edge-secret calls (e.g. DB triggers) are unchanged. ## Deploy note Deploy the updated `autograder-create-repos-for-student` edge function for this fix to apply in production.
  
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Test assignments can now create individual student repositories even when an assignment is configured as group-only. * The "Create Student Repos" action/button now supports a "Test Assignment" mode, enabling instructors to trigger the alternate repo-creation flow from assignment pages.

author: hai-pilgrim
body:
## Summary

Addresses item 4 from issue #6 (Performance: training pipeline optimizations).

Previously `training_step` called `_generate_trajectory` in a Python loop, issuing one `model.generate` call per (message × trajectory) pair — `B × T` GPU round trips per step. This PR replaces that loop with a single batched call.

### Changes

- Added `_generate_trajectories_batched(user_messages, num_trajectories)` to `PromptBakingTrainer`
  - Repeats each user message `num_trajectories` times
  - Tokenizes all prompts with **left-padding** (required for generation so real tokens align at the right)
  - Issues one `model.generate` call for the entire batch
  - Decodes and pairs outputs back to source messages, filtering empty responses
  - Returns early on empty input without touching the tokenizer
- Updated `training_step` to call `_generate_trajectories_batched` instead of the sequential loop

### Impact

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| batch_size=1, num_traj=4 | 4 generate calls | 1 generate call |
| batch_size=4, num_traj=4 | 16 generate calls | 1 generate call |

The speedup is most significant when `batch_size > 1` or `num_trajectories > 1`, which are the common configurations.

## Test plan

- [x] 5 new tests: pair types, message identity, trajectory repeat count, empty input guard, empty-response filtering
- [x] All 13 trainer tests pass

author: ivan-marchand
body:
## Summary

- **`uart.txdone()` → `uart.any()`**: `txdone()` checks if the TX buffer is empty; `any()` correctly checks for incoming RX data — the main loop was only reading when it had nothing to transmit, which is backwards
- **`pos > 0` → `pos >= 0`** in buffer parser: a leading `\n` (e.g. from line endings) would stall the parser forever since `pos == 0` triggered `break` instead of advancing the buffer
- **PID anti-windup**: clamp `integration_sum` to `±(100 / ki)` to prevent the integrator from winding up when the motor is stalled or target is far away
- **IRQ-safe counter snapshot**: wrap `left_step_counter` / `right_step_counter` reads in `disable_irq()`/`enable_irq()` to prevent a torn read mid-interrupt
- **Dead zone**: add configurable `dead_zone` (default 0, sent as optional 8th arg in `M:C:...` command); applied at PWM output as `dead_zone + (100 - dead_zone) * duty / 100` so the full PID range maps to `[dead_zone, 100]%` PWM
- **Remove dead assignment**: `ref_speed = speed` immediately overwrote `ref_speed = abs(left_ref_speed + right_ref_speed) / 2`, breaking braking distance calculations
- **Typo fixes**: `Unknonw` → `Unknown` in `[Servo]`, `[Battery]`, and `[UltraSonic]` error messages; `[Servo]` prefix corrected to `[UltraSonic]` in UltraSonicHandler

## Test plan

- [ ] Deploy `pico/main.py` to the Pico and verify motors initialize correctly
- [ ] Drive forward/back and confirm PID settles without oscillation
- [ ] Verify dead zone has no effect when `motor_dead_zone` config key is absent (default 0)
- [ ] Set `motor_dead_zone` config and confirm motors spin at low commanded speeds
- [ ] Verify patroller still stops when obstacle detected

author: copilot
body:
Files uploaded directly to a Telegram storage channel bypass TelDrive's database entirely, making them invisible in the UI. This adds a `POST /users/channels/{id}/import` endpoint that walks the channel history and registers any untracked document messages as TelDrive file records.

## API

**`POST /users/channels/{id}/import`**

Request body (`ChannelImport`):
```json
{ "path": "/root/imports" }
```
- `path` — destination folder in TelDrive (created if absent, defaults to `/root`)

Response (`ImportResult`):
```json
{ "imported": 42, "total": 150 }
```

## Implementation

- **`openapi/openapi.json`** — new endpoint + `ChannelImport` / `ImportResult` schemas; `internal/api` is regenerated from the spec at build time
- **`pkg/services/user.go`** — `UsersImportChannel`:
  - Pre-fetches all Telegram message IDs already in `teldrive.files` for the channel (via JSONB query on `parts`) to cheaply skip already-imported messages
  - Iterates the full channel history with `GetHistory` (100 msg/page)
  - Extracts filename from `DocumentAttributeFilename`, MIME type and size from the document object; falls back to `file_<msg_id>` / `application/octet-stream` when absent
  - Inserts each new file with the same `ON CONFLICT (name, COALESCE(parent_id,…), user_id) WHERE status='active' DO NOTHING` raw SQL used in `FilesCreate` to respect the partial unique index
  - Marks imported files as unencrypted (`encrypted=false`) since direct Telegram uploads are plaintext

body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** Subagent command handling logic (~1100 LOC across 11 action files) was monolithic in `handlers/commands_subagents_*.go`, making it difficult to test, maintain, and reuse independently.
- **Why it matters:** Separating domain logic from HTTP handler concerns improves testability, reduces coupling, and enables cleaner architecture.
- **What changed:** Extracted all subagent command action handlers, utilities, and ACP wiring into a new `internal/autoreply/subagent/` package with dedicated modules (`actions.go`, `dispatch.go`, `acp_wiring.go`, `run_utils.go`). The `handlers` package now re-exports types and delegates to the subagent package via thin facades.
- **What did NOT change:** Public API contracts, command behavior, or test coverage. All existing handler entry points remain in `handlers/` and work identically.

## Change Type

- [x] Refactor

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related: Subagent command architecture cleanup

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None. All `/subagents`, `/kill`, `/steer`, `/tell`, `/focus`, `/unfocus`, and `/agents` commands behave identically.

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? **No**
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? **No**
- New/changed network calls? **No**
- Command/tool execution surface changed? **No**
- Data access scope changed? **No**

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- Go 1.18+
- Existing test suite

### Steps

1. Run `go test ./internal/autoreply/subagent/...` to verify new package tests
2. Run `go test ./internal/autoreply/handlers/...` to verify handler facades still work
3. Verify no import cycles: `go build ./...`

### Expected

- All tests pass
- No import cycles
- Handler facades delegate correctly to subagent package

### Actual

- ✅ Tests pass (dispatch_test.go, acp_wiring_test.go added to subagent package)
- ✅ No import cycles
- ✅ Facades in handlers/ re-export and delegate

## Evidence

- [x] Existing tests pass (moved to `internal/autoreply/subagent/dispatch_test.go` and `acp_wiring_test.go`)
- [x] New package structure compiles without errors
- [x] Handler facades correctly delegate to subagent package implementations

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios:**
  - Subagent command dispatch logic works identically via new package
  - ACP wiring correctly bridges registry to command deps
  - All action handlers (help, list, kill, info, log, send, steer, spawn, focus, unfocus, agents) execute as before
  
- **Edge cases checked:**
  - Empty run lists
  - Missing dependencies (graceful fallback)
  - Target resolution by index, label, and run ID prefix
  
- **What was NOT verified:**
  - End-to-end integration with live ACP registry (covered by existing integration tests)
  - User-facing command output formatting (unchanged, covered by moved tests)

## Compatibility / Migration

- **Backward compatible?** Yes. All public APIs in `handlers/` remain unchanged; internal implementation moved.
- **Config/env changes?** No
- **Migration needed?** No

## Failure Recovery

- **How to revert:** `git revert <commit>` restores original monolithic structure
- **Files to restore:** `handlers/commands_subagents*.go` (original versions)
- **Known bad symptoms:** Import errors if subagent package is not built; handler facades would fail if subagent package is deleted

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk:** Import cycle if subagent package imports from handlers
  - **Mitigation:** Subagent package only imports from `acp` and `session` packages; handlers imports subagent (one-way dependency)

- **Risk:** Missed refactoring of utility functions
  - **Mitigation:**

Updates the CODEOWNERS file to allow the on-call team to approve dependency-related file changes, such as those from Dependabot PRs.

## Changes

- Added on-call team (`@radius-project/on-call`) as code owners for:

### Motivation
- Unify input ingestion paths behind a single facade and migrate the app away from legacy ingest helpers so paste/file/url inputs use the same normalization pipeline. 
- Surface ingestion failures to the UI so users see clear warnings when extraction or parsing fails.

### Description
- Replaced legacy imports from `src/lib/ingest/ingest` with `ingestInput` from `src/features/ingest/urlAdapter.ts` in `src/App.tsx` and removed the unused `pitch` state. 
- Refactored `runIngest` to call `ingestInput` with the shaped requests `ingestInput({ type: 'paste', payload: textInput })`, `ingestInput({ type: 'file', payload: selectedFile })`, and `ingestInput({ type: 'url', payload: urlInput })`. 
- Added a `toDocumentModel` adapter that maps `NormalizedDocument` (domain shape) into the UI's existing `DocumentModel` shape and maps block types to the old segment types. 
- Added `try/catch` around ingestion to populate `documentModel.warnings` with an `INGEST_ERROR` when ingestion fails, and reset the current segment index to keep the UI stable. 
- Removed the now-obsolete `src/lib/ingest/ingest.ts` file after migrating `App.tsx` to the new facade.

### Testing
- Ran the project build via `npm run build` (which invokes `tsc -b && vite build`) and observed the build fail due to pre-existing TypeScript/module declaration issues in preview sanitizer files, which are unrelated to this ingestion refactor.

body:
⏺ What changed

  Replaced manual offset-based pagination with Jetpack Paging 3. The blog list previously tracked page numbers in the ViewModel, detected end-of-pagination by parsing an API error
   string ("Invalid page."), and triggered loads via a RecyclerView scroll listener. All of that is replaced by a Pager + RemoteMediator + PagingDataAdapter pipeline.
                                                                                                                                                                                   
  New data layer:                                                                                                                                                                  
  - BlogRemoteKey entity and BlogRemoteKeyDao track the next page to fetch per search+filter combination.
  - BlogRemoteMediator handles API fetch and Room insert. On REFRESH it re-fetches page 1; on APPEND it loads the next page. It includes a 5-minute staleness check in initialize()
   to skip redundant network calls when data is fresh. Offline, REFRESH shows cached data silently while APPEND shows an error footer with retry.                                  
  - BlogPostDao replaces five separate ordered query methods with a single @RawQuery returning PagingSource<Int, BlogPost>. Room handles LIMIT/OFFSET internally.                  
  - BlogQueryUtils builds the dynamic SQL query with the correct ORDER BY clause via SimpleSQLiteQuery.                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                   
  Updated repository + use case:                                                                                                                                                   
  - BlogRepository.searchBlogPosts(query, filter, page): Flow<Resource<BlogSearchResult>> replaced by getBlogPagingData(query, filter): Flow<PagingData<BlogPost>>. Page numbers   
  are managed internally by the Pager.                                                                                                                                             
  - BlogRepositoryImpl creates a Pager with PagingConfig, BlogRemoteMediator, and a Room PagingSource factory. It now injects AppDatabase instead of BlogPostDao (the DAO is
  derived from the database).                                                                                                                                                      
  - SearchBlogPostsUseCase drops the page parameter.                                                                                                                               
   
  Simplified ViewModel:                                                                                                                                                            
  - BlogViewModel exposes pagingDataFlow: Flow<PagingData<BlogPost>> built from flatMapLatest on a searchParams StateFlow, cached with cachedIn(viewModelScope). The initial
  searchParams is null and only emits after executeSearch() in init, avoiding a wasted Pager creation.                                                                             
  - Removed: loadFirstPage(), nextPage(), searchBlogPosts(), handleIncomingBlogListData(), removeDeletedBlogPost(), updateListItem(), setBlogListData(), setQueryExhausted(),
  setQueryInProgress(), setLayoutManagerState(), and all associated state fields.                                                                                                  
  - After delete/update, Room auto-invalidates the PagingSource — no manual list manipulation needed.                                                                              
                                                                                                     
  Converted UI layer:                                                                                                                                                              
  - BlogListAdapter extends PagingDataAdapter instead of RecyclerView.Adapter + AsyncListDiffer. The NO_MORE_RESULTS marker view type and GenericViewHolder are gone.              
  - New BlogLoadStateAdapter shows a progress spinner or "Something went wrong" + retry button as a footer.                                                                        
  - BlogFragment collects pagingDataFlow with collectLatest + submitData, observes loadStateFlow to drive the swipe-refresh indicator, and uses withLoadStateFooter for the footer 
  adapter. The scroll listener is removed.                                                                                                                                         
  - BlogListUiState retains only searchQuery, filter, and order. The layoutManagerState field was removed since cachedIn preserves scroll position across config changes.          
                                                                                                                                                                                   
  Deleted:                                                                                                                                                                         
  - BlogSearchResult.kt (replaced by PagingData), GenericViewHolder.kt (only used for NO_MORE_RESULTS), layout_no_more_results.xml (replaced by layout_blog_load_state.xml), empty
  domain/model/ directory.                                                                                                                                                         
                  
  Why this approach                                                                                                                                                                
                  
  RemoteMediator + Room PagingSource, not PagingSource-only. A network-only PagingSource would lose offline support and require re-fetching all data on every configuration change.
   With RemoteMediator, Room is the single source of truth: data is fetched once from the API, persisted locally, and the Room-backed PagingSource handles display with automatic
  invalidation on table changes. This also means deleting or updating a blog post on the detail screen automatically refreshes the list — no manual removeDeletedBlogPost() or     
  updateListItem() needed.

  @RawQuery for dynamic ordering. The app supports 4 sort orders (date ASC/DESC, author ASC/DESC). Without @RawQuery, we'd need 4 separate DAO methods each returning              
  PagingSource<Int, BlogPost> — identical except for the ORDER BY clause. A single @RawQuery with SimpleSQLiteQuery eliminates the duplication. Room's observedEntities annotation
  ensures invalidation still works.                                                                                                                                                
                  
  Remote key per query, not per item. The API uses page numbers (not cursors), so a single BlogRemoteKey row per search+filter combination is sufficient. Per-item remote keys are 
  for cursor-based APIs and would be unnecessarily complex here.
                                                                                                                                                                                   
  No table clear on REFRESH. All blog posts live in one Room table regardless of search query. Clearing the table on refresh would destroy cached data from other searches.        
  Instead, the Room PagingSource applies a WHERE clause to filter posts, and the RemoteMediator only clears the remote key to force re-fetching page 1.

author: adamshiervani
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: `keypressReport` performed a read-modify-write on `keysDownState` across three separate lock acquisitions. Concurrent callers (two auto-release timers firing simultaneously, or an auto-release racing with a session-disconnect `KeyboardReport(0, zeros)`) could interleave — each reading the same stale state, computing a partial mutation, and the last writer winning with one key still "held".

- **Fix**: Replace the per-write `keyboardWriteHidFileLock` with a `keyboardMutex` that covers the entire read→compute→write→update sequence in both `keypressReport` and `KeyboardReport`. All keyboard state mutations are now serialisable, eliminating the race by construction.

- Also cancel pending auto-release timers on session close (avoids unnecessary HID writes after the clear) and query device key state directly via JSON-RPC in the E2E test (removes Zustand store timing dependency).

## Test plan

- [x] `keyboard: all keys released when WebRTC session disconnects` — 10/10 passes (was ~1-in-10 failure before fix)
- [x] Full E2E suite (43 tests) passes

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches concurrency and teardown paths in USB HID keyboard reporting; mistakes could cause dropped or stuck key events, but changes are localized and covered by E2E validation updates.
> 
> **Overview**
> Prevents stuck keys by **serializing the full keyboard read→compute→HID write→state update sequence** with a new `keyboardMutex`, replacing the prior per-write lock and eliminating races between concurrent key events (including auto-release timers).
> 
> On WebRTC session close, the device now **cancels all pending keyboard auto-release timers** before sending the all-keys-up report, ensuring no late timer can reintroduce stale key state. The E2E disconnect test is updated to **query keys-down state via JSON-RPC** (instead of UI hook/Zustand timing) to make the assertion deterministic.
>

body:
## Summary                                                                                                                                            
                                         
  Restructures the `plan` command from a single-pass prompt into a multi-phase orchestration inspired by the RPI (Research, Plan, Implement) pattern.   
  The core insight: most build-phase token consumption comes from the agent discovering codebase reality during implementation. This change front-loads
  that work into research and planning, making build mechanical.                                                                                        
                                                            
  ## What changed

  **New plan lifecycle** (`ralph plan` now runs 4 internal phases):

  1. **Assessment** — Picks the next spec, reads it, determines complexity tier (light/medium/heavy)                                                    
  2. **Research** — Spawns 1-4 parallel sub-agents (based on tier) to explore the codebase. Writes factual findings to `research.md` — no suggestions,
  only grounded observations with file paths and line numbers                                                                                           
  3. **Planning** — Fresh context: reads spec + research.md, generates atomic tasks detailed enough for mechanical execution
  4. **Validation + Reflection** — Haiku scores the plan on 6 criteria (0-10 each). If below tier threshold (85/90/92%), Opus refines the plan. Loops up
   to `max_reflections` times (default 3). Pink warning if threshold not met after max attempts                                                         
                                                                                                                                                        
  **Removed artifacts:**                                                                                                                                
  - `design.md` — replaced by `research.md` (codebase reality) + richer implementation plan (design decisions)
  - `_interview.md` — spec interview now uses a temp file, cleaned up when done

author: kevenabraham
body:
## Summary

This PR adds support for multi-turn tool use in the Claude API integration, enabling the LLM to invoke local device actions (open apps, open URLs) in a loop until producing a final response. It also introduces cross-platform app launching with macOS and Linux support, and enhances the system prompt with a more personalized assistant persona.

## Key Changes

- **Multi-turn tool use loop**: Implemented `CompleteWithTools()` in ClaudeClient that handles iterative tool invocations, persisting tool_use/tool_result messages for future context
- **Cross-platform app launching**: 
  - Added macOS support via `open -a` with app name resolution (handles voice transcription variants like "crome" → "Google Chrome")
  - Added Linux support with fallback browser detection (xdg-open, sensible-browser, firefox, etc.)
  - Implemented URL opening for both platforms
- **Tool message persistence**: Extended the message model with `RoleToolUse` and `RoleToolResult` roles, added database migration to support these new roles
- **Context builder integration**: Introduced `ContextBuilder` service to inject system prompt and memories into conversation context
- **Enhanced system prompt**: Replaced generic prompt with "Vega" persona — a casual, opinionated AI assistant that speaks natural Portuguese BR without robotic phrases
- **Action executor refactor**: Unified tool handling through `HandleTool()` entry point that dispatches to platform-specific implementations
- **UUID generation**: Added crypto/rand-based UUID v4 generation for conversation and message IDs (no external dependencies)
- **Dependency injection**: Updated Fx modules and use case constructors to wire ContextBuilder and ActionExecutor

## Notable Implementation Details

- Tool results are stored as JSON in message content for reconstruction during API calls
- The tool use loop appends assistant messages unconditionally to maintain context, then executes tool calls and sends results back
- App name resolution uses normalized (lowercased, trimmed) lookups with fallback to title-cased names
- System prompt is loaded from disk at startup and injected into every API request
- Conversation save errors are logged but don't fail the request (graceful degradation)

Upgrade Starlette to fix DoS vulnerability from unbounded multipart form buffering and event loop blocking during large file uploads.
✅ Code not affected by breaking changes.
No breaking changes from the Starlette upgrade affect this codebase. The codebase uses FastAPI (which depends on Starlette), but none of the breaking changes impact the actual code: - No direct usage of `MultiPartParser`, `max_part_size`, or `max_file_size`/`spool_max_size` - No usage of `TestClient` or `allow_redirects` parameter - No imports from `starlette.exceptions` or usage of `ExceptionMiddleware` - No usage of deprecated WebSocket constants `WS_1004_NO_STATUS_RCVD` or `WS_1005_ABNORMAL_CLOSURE` - No explicit `methods` parameter usage that would be affected by the type change - The application only uses simple FastAPI decorators (`@app.get()` and `@app.post()`) with JSON request/response bodies The upgrade should be safe as the codebase doesn't directly interact with any of the changed Starlette APIs. body:
### Summary of Changes

This pull request addresses two key areas related to the skill tree UI:

1.  **Function Call Reordering:** The `drawSkillConnections()` function call has been moved to execute *before* `updateSkillTreeLockStates()` in two distinct locations within `index.html`. This reordering occurs both in the initial skill tree setup logic and within the `window.refreshSkillTreeUI` function.
2.  **Refined Class Reset Logic:** The logic for resetting dynamic styles and classes on skill nodes has been updated. Specifically, the `highlighted` class is no longer removed during a general reset, ensuring its state is preserved if managed independently.

### Technical Impact

*   **Dependency Resolution:** By ensuring `drawSkillConnections()` is called prior to `updateSkillTreeLockStates()`, the `skillNodes` data structure is guaranteed to be fully populated before `updateSkillTreeLockStates()` attempts to evaluate and apply lock states. This resolves a critical dependency, preventing potential issues where lock states might be incorrectly calculated based on incomplete or outdated skill node information.
*   **Accurate UI State Management:** The modification to the class reset logic ensures that the `highlighted` state of a skill node persists as intended across UI updates. This prevents unintended visual flickers or loss of highlighting, leading to a more consistent and predictable user experience, especially when highlighting is used for temporary visual cues or selections.
*   **Enhanced Robustness:** These changes collectively improve the overall robustness and reliability of the skill tree UI rendering, reducing the likelihood of visual glitches, incorrect lock state displays, or unexpected behavior during user interaction and UI refreshes.

NFTs minted using Pinata's `proton.mypinata.cloud` and `agent.mypinata.cloud` gateways are not displaying on nft.xprnetwork.org or in the WebAuth wallet. The IPFS content is accessible but Next.js blocks the images because these domains are not whitelisted.

- `proton.mypinata.cloud` — used by `IPFS_RESOLVER_IMAGE` in constants.ts
- `agent.mypinata.cloud` — used by nft.charliebot.dev and other tools
- `simplelaunch.mypinata.cloud` — used by SimpleDEX token images

## Testing

Verified that IPFS hashes are accessible via these gateways (HTTP 200). After this fix, NFT images from chainportra2 and other collections using these gateways will display correctly.

author: mircovalentiniecmwf
body:
### Description

## Summary

This draft PR introduces a first staged-encoding path for `mars2grib`, together with the minimal API exposure needed to exercise it from the current public interface.

The main goal is **not** to finalize the cache design yet, but to prepare the codebase for the cache mechanism that will be implemented shortly and, in the meantime, enable comparison against the existing well-tested cache-based workflow.

## What is included

### `SpecializedEncoder`

Added two new staged methods:

* `prepare(...)`
* `finaliseEncoding(...)`

These split the current hot-path header generation into:

* a **preparation phase**, producing an immutable prepared sample
* a **finalisation phase**, cloning the prepared sample and applying only the runtime stage

The existing `encode(...)` path remains unchanged.

### `CoreOperations`

Added a first staged workflow on top of the encoder:

* `CoreOperations::CacheEntry`
* `CoreOperations::prepare(...)`
* `CoreOperations::finaliseEncoding(...)`

This path mirrors the existing normalization / layout resolution / header encoding / value injection flow, but exposes the intermediate prepared cache object explicitly.

This is intended as a **transitional step** toward a future implementation where cache lifecycle and reuse will be fully internalized inside the core layer.

### `Mars2Grib` API

Added temporary public exposure of the staged path:

* opaque `CacheEntry`
* `prepare(...)`
* `finaliseEncoding(...)`

The public API remains specialized on:

* `eckit::LocalConfiguration`
* `Options`
* `metkit::codes::CodesHandle`

The public cache object is only a thin opaque wrapper around the current core cache entry.

## Important note

This PR does **not** claim that the staged cache API is final.

The newly exposed staged functions are temporary and are only here to:

1. reuse the old, already tested cache-oriented logic,
2. run performance comparisons,
3. prepare the refactoring that will soon move the full cache management inside the core layer.

So the intention of this PR is mainly:

* architectural preparation,
* controlled incremental migration,
* benchmarking support.

## Non-goals

This PR does **not** aim to:

* finalize the public staged API,
* freeze cache semantics,
* complete the future internal cache implementation.

## Expected next step

A follow-up step should replace this temporary staged exposure with a cleaner internal cache design managed entirely in `CoreOperations`, while preserving or simplifying the public API accordingly.

## Remarks

A few naming inconsistencies remain in the code (`par` / `misc`) because this terminology has changed multiple times during the design discussions and is already spread across the existing codebase. I preferred not to do a large naming cleanup in this PR in order to keep the change focused on the staged/cache preparation itself.


### Contributor Declaration

By opening this pull request, I affirm the following:

* All authors agree to the [Contributor License Agreement](https://github.com/ecmwf/codex/blob/main/Legal/contributor_license_agreement.md).
* The code follows the project's coding standards.
* I have performed self-review and added comments where needed.
* I have added or updated tests to verify that my changes are effective and functional.
* I have run all existing tests and confirmed they pass.

## Summary
- Restructure `CMapHit::CalcHitPosition` so each branch performs its own `PSVECAdd` after scaling the hit direction.

- Duplicating the final `PSVECAdd` in each branch is a normal source-level structure for two slightly different scale calculations.

author: dustin-dowell
body:
## Summary
- Add `--node-ip=$TS_IP` to install.sh COMMON_ARGS

## Context
PR #166 switched flannel from `--flannel-iface=tailscale0` to `--flannel-backend=wireguard-native`. Without the flannel interface directive, K3s auto-detects the default interface (eth0) and uses its physical LAN IP for internal communication — including the etcd peer URL health check.

This caused tpi2 to enter an infinite etcd defragmentation loop because etcd members are registered with Tailscale IPs (100.x.x.x) but K3s expected the physical IP (192.168.1.211). The API server was unavailable during defrag cycles.

`--node-ip=$TS_IP` explicitly tells K3s which IP to use for all internal communication, preventing the mismatch.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI deploys successfully (site.yml runs without etcd errors)
- [ ] `kubectl get nodes` shows all nodes Ready
- [ ] No "not a member of the etcd cluster" errors in K3s logs

author: svarlamov
body:
## Summary

Optimizes the rebase authorship rewrite with two major changes:

1. **Hunk-based attribution reconstruction** — replaces expensive content-based matching (cat-file per commit) with replay of diff-tree hunks to shift line attributions forward through commit history
2. **Combined diff-tree subprocess** — merges the two separate git diff-tree calls (new commits + original commits) into a single `--stdin` invocation, eliminating ~500ms of process startup overhead

### Key optimizations

- **Hunk-based attribution reconstruction** (attribution_reconstruction: 906ms → 6ms, **150x**):
  Instead of reading file contents at every original commit via cat-file and doing content-based matching, replay diff-tree hunks forward to shift accumulated attributions. Each commit's note only covers lines changed in that commit, so we overlay note ranges onto the running attribution state.

- **Combined diff-tree call** (diff_tree: 594ms + 587ms → single call):
  Both new-commit and original-commit diff-tree calls use identical flags (`--stdin --raw -p -U0`). Concatenate both commit lists into one stdin pipe, partition results afterward.

- **Per-commit metrics recomputation**: Fixed bug where `prompt_line_metrics` were frozen before the commit loop, causing all rebased commits to share identical accepted_lines/overridden_lines values. Now recomputed per commit.

- **Delete-then-recreate** bug fixes: Clear `seen_files`, `files_with_synced_state`, `current_file_contents`, and `current_attributions` when a file is deleted, preventing stale data from corrupting attributions on re-creation.

### Benchmark results (realistic monorepo benchmark — 2000 files, 8 AI-tracked, 30 feature onto 500 main)

| Metric | Standard `git rebase` | Graphite-style (commit-tree + update-ref) |
|---|---|---|
| **Total wall clock** | 0.933s | 1.445s |
| **git-ai internal** | 165ms | 235ms |
| **Per feature commit** | 31.1ms | 48.1ms |
| **Notes rewritten** | 531→561 (30 new) | 531→561 (30 new) |

#### Phase timing comparison

| Phase | Standard | Graphite | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| load_rebase_note_cache | 10ms | 68ms | +58ms (history walk) |
| diff_tree_combined | 34ms | 24ms | -10ms |
| attribution_reconstruction | 4ms | 4ms | — |
| commit_processing_loop | 51ms | 51ms | — |
| notes_add_batch | 51ms | 77ms | +26ms |
| **TOTAL** | **165ms** | **235ms** | **+70ms (+42%)** |

The Graphite path's overhead is entirely in `load_rebase_note_cache` (history walking to reconstruct commit mappings — standard rebase gets these for free from git's rewritten-list file). The core processing loop is identical.

### Test results
- 3064+ integration tests: all pass
- New `test_graphite_style_multi_commit_single_update_ref` — verifies N notes remapped from single update-ref
- New `test_rebase_file_delete_recreate_after_hunk_modification` — exercises create→hunk-modify→delete→recreate sequence
- Graphite-style benchmark matching actual `gt sync` behavior (commit-tree replay + atomic update-ref)

author: dallasheidt14
body:
Fixes three match predictor issues identified in the audit improvements backlog.

**Non-monotonic calibration curve:** The hardcoded calibration points were non-monotonic (e.g., 62.5% raw mapped to 73.9% calibrated, but 72.5% raw mapped to only 65.0%). Applied pool-adjacent-violators (PAV) to enforce monotonicity so stronger predictions always produce higher win probabilities.

**Triple mismatch amplification:** Mismatch score was being applied in three places: compositeDiff amplification (1.8x), dampening removal in getAgeSpecificMarginMultiplier, and a third mismatchMarginBoost (2.2x). Total effect was ~4.1x, band-aided by an 8-goal cap. Removed the third application and the cap since the first two already account for mismatches correctly.

**H2H coefficient:** Reduced from `* 10` to `* 3`. The previous scaling made H2H 4.2x more influential than a significant power gap with zero empirical validation. With typical 2-3 game sample sizes this was overfitting to H2H noise.

author: dglazkov
body:
## What
Introduces a new ticket kind (`coordination`) that enables agents to emit typed signals mid-session, which the scheduler durably delivers to subscribing agents via the existing `watch_events` / `context_updates` channel.

## Why
Agents need a way to pass information to each other without spawning new work sessions. The existing `playbook_complete` watcher mechanism only fires at playbook completion and is hardcoded to that single event type. Coordination tickets generalize this into an agent-callable, typed, durable signal with delivery tracking.

## Changes

### Ticket model (`ticket.py`)
- New `kind` field: `"work"` (default) or `"coordination"`
- New `signal_type` field: routing key for coordination signals
- New `delivered_to` field: tracks which subscribers have received the signal

### Coordination function group (new)
- `coordination.functions.json`, `coordination.instruction.md`, `coordination.metadata.json`
- `coordination.py` handler: `coordination_emit(signal_type, context)` creates a coordination ticket and triggers the scheduler

### Scheduler (`scheduler.py`)
- Extracted `_deliver_signal(signal_type, payload, source_tags)` from `_deliver_to_watchers`, generalizing signal routing for both `playbook_complete` and coordination signals
- New `_route_coordination_ticket`: durable delivery — ticket stays `available` until all matching subscribers have been delivered to, retries busy subscribers next cycle, survives server restarts
- Updated `_run_cycles` and `run_all_waves` to split coordination vs work tickets
- Added `on_coordination_emit` to `SchedulerHooks`
- Fixed stale-data overwrite in `_handle_suspend`: reloads `queued_updates` from disk before checking

### Session + server wiring
- `on_coordination_emit` callback threaded through `run_session`/`resume_session`
- Server broadcasts `ticket_added` on coordination emit, `ticket_update` on routing progress

### Devtools UI
- Coordination tickets display `signal_type` pill + `context` text instead of empty objective
- "coordination" badge in ticket header
- `TicketData` type extended with `kind`, `signal_type`, `context`

### Test playbooks
- `test/PLAYBOOK.yaml`: emitter that sends 4 seasonal `test_update` signals
- `rendering/PLAYBOOK.yaml`: listener that writes poems about received updates

## Testing
1. Run `npm run dev -w packages/bees`
2. Run the "rendering" playbook (creates a listener agent)
3. Run the "test" playbook (emits 4 coordination signals)
4. Verify: all 4 coordination tickets appear in devtools, transition from `available` → `completed`, and the rendering agent writes 4 poems (one per season)

## Changes provided by this PR

This PR fixes the suggestion **[S5043] Node.js built-in modules should be required/imported using the node: prefix** reported by the ioBroker repository checker.

### Background

Starting with Node.js 14.18.0 / 16.0.0, built-in modules can be imported using the `node:` URL scheme (e.g., `require('node:fs')` instead of `require('fs')`). This is now the recommended way to reference built-in modules because:

- It makes it immediately clear that the import is a Node.js built-in module and not a third-party package
- It avoids potential naming conflicts with npm packages that have the same name as built-ins
- It improves code readability and maintainability
- It is the modern Node.js best practice recommended by the Node.js project

### Changes

This PR updates all `require()` calls, `import ... from` statements, and dynamic `import()` calls in the adapter source files to use the `node:` prefix for Node.js built-in modules.

For example:
- `require('fs')` → `require('node:fs')`
- `require('path')` → `require('node:path')`
- `import fs from 'fs'` → `import fs from 'node:fs'`
- `import { readFile } from 'fs'` → `import { readFile } from 'node:fs'`

The following directories and files are excluded from the scan:
- Directories: `admin`, `build`, `doc`, `src-admin`, `src-widgets`, `admin-src`, `test`, `node_modules`, `.git`, `.vscode`, `.dev-server`

author: cloutiertyler
body:
## Summary

Implements pipelined two-phase commit for distributed transactions between SpacetimeDB databases. A coordinator database can call a reducer on a participant database via `call_reducer_on_db_2pc`, and the runtime guarantees that either both sides commit or neither does.

- **Participant side**: New HTTP endpoints (`/prepare/:reducer`, `/2pc/commit/:id`, `/2pc/abort/:id`) and `PreparedTransactions` registry on `ModuleHost`
- **Coordinator side**: New `call_reducer_on_db_2pc` host function (ABI `spacetime_10.5`) that calls the participant's prepare endpoint, with automatic post-commit coordination (sends commit to all participants on success, abort on failure)
- **Bindings**: FFI and safe wrapper for `call_reducer_on_db_2pc`
- **Smoketests**: Happy path (atomic transfer between two databases) and abort path (insufficient funds rolls back both sides)

## Protocol flow

1. Coordinator's reducer calls `call_reducer_on_db_2pc(target, "debit", args)`
2. Runtime POSTs to participant's `/prepare/debit` endpoint
3. Participant executes reducer, commits in-memory, returns result + prepare_id
4. Coordinator's reducer continues with the result
5. On coordinator commit: runtime sends `/2pc/commit/{id}` to all participants
6. On coordinator failure: runtime sends `/2pc/abort/{id}` to all participants

## Prototype scope cuts

- No persistence barrier (speculative transactions persist normally)
- COMMIT on participant is a no-op (data already committed during prepare)
- ABORT does not invert in-memory state (logs warning)
- No crash recovery or PREPARE/COMMIT/ABORT commitlog record types
- No commitlog recording of remote return values (replayability deferred)

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p spacetimedb-standalone` compiles
- [x] `test_cross_db_2pc_happy_path` -- transfer 50 between databases, verify both updated
- [x] `test_cross_db_2pc_abort_insufficient_funds` -- transfer 200 with only 100 available, verify both unchanged

body:
## 💡 What
Added a standard `Tooltip` widget around the "Home" icon in the breadcrumb navigation. Additionally, wrapped the application title inside an `Expanded` widget and removed `mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min` from the App Title row to prevent a `RenderFlex` overflow issue.

## 🎯 Why
Icon-only interactive elements without labels are inaccessible to screen readers and difficult to understand for new users. Adding a tooltip provides both an on-hover text hint and proper semantic labeling.
The layout fix resolves a failing widget test caused by `RenderFlex overflowed by 49 pixels on the right` due to strict constraints on smaller viewports.

## 📸 Before/After
**Before:**
The home button in the breadcrumb (`Icons.home_rounded`) lacked any hover state or accessibility label. The App title could overflow on constrained viewports (like in widget tests), causing rendering exceptions.

**After:**
Hovering over the home button displays "Home", and screen readers announce it as such. The App title gracefully handles overflow using an ellipsis, keeping layouts intact and widget tests passing.

## ♿ Accessibility
This explicitly addresses WCAG guidelines for labeling icon-only buttons. The `Tooltip` widget automatically handles ARIA-equivalent semantics in Flutter Web and native screen reader bindings on iOS/Android.

body:
## Purpose From profiling trace it seemed like DeepEP HT backend wasn't fully overlapping the compute and communication. The only thing being overlapped is one of the ubatch combine with the other ubatch non-moe compute. Going through the DBO code it seems that the core issue is the `previous_event` that is passed to DeepEP dispatch/combine. The way it's implemented, DeepEP will wait for the entire compute stream to finish before launching dispatch. Since we have yielded via `dbo_yield_and_switch_from_compute_to_comm()` right before this point, the compute stream will contain compute enqueued by the other ubatch that the current ubatch doesn't need to depend on. The fix is to move the DeepEP event capture right before yield so it correctly captures the compute tail of the current ubatch. author: drothermel
body:
## Summary

Restructures catalog/, storage/, and pool/ into a clean two-flow architecture:

- **Flow 1 (standalone):** `providers/` + `catalog/` — call models, sync/browse catalogs. File-based persistence, no Postgres dependency.
- **Flow 2 (pool):** `pool/` — absorbs all Postgres infrastructure (runtime, call recording, schema, migrations). Sample pools, pending lifecycle, run tracking.

## Changes

- **Delete `client.py`** — CLI commands call providers and catalog service directly
- **File-based catalog** — replace Postgres-backed `_catalog_store.py` with `catalog/file_store.py` (JSON per provider at `~/.dr_llm/catalog_cache/`)
- **Dissolve `storage/`** — runtime, call recorder, schema SQL, migrations all move into `pool/`. Rename `StorageConfig`→`DbConfig`, `StorageRuntime`→`DbRuntime`, `PostgresRepository`→`PoolDb`
- **Split `PoolStore`** — extract `PendingStore`, `MetadataStore`, and `sql_helpers.py` from 1086-line monolith
- **Reorganize tests** — split 464-line `test_cli.py` into per-command files, move tests into subdirs matching source structure (`tests/cli/`, `tests/catalog/`, `tests/pool/`, etc.)
- **Fix bugs** — `ContainerStatus` crash on Docker `"exited"`, `models list` missing file store
- **Clean up scripts** — fix broken paths, remove stale `demo-query-flow.sh`, add usage docs
- **Rewrite README** — reflects two-flow architecture, accurate examples and CLI reference

## Final structure

```
src/dr_llm/
├── catalog/          # Flow 1: file-based model catalog
│   ├── file_store.py

author: toddr-bot
body:
## What

Reverts two commits that broke downstream CPAN modules: the defaulthandle→Char routing (70ad8fe) and the XMLDecl standalone string change (9c28019).

## Why

Three open issues (GH#211, GH#212, GH#213) report that XML-Twig, XML-DOM, and XML-XPath test suites fail against XML-Parser 2.48+. Bisection traces to these two commits:

1. **defaulthandle char routing** (GH#47 fix): intended to forward post-root-element character data from Default to Char, but the heuristic (`string[0] != '<' && string[0] != '&'`) catches ALL non-markup data going through Default — including DTD prolog whitespace, parameter entity content, etc. This caused 34 extra test failures in XML-Twig alone.

2. **XMLDecl standalone strings** (GH#73 fix): changed standalone from Perl booleans (`PL_sv_yes`/`PL_sv_no`) to literal `"yes"`/`"no"` strings. The string `"no"` is truthy in Perl, breaking the `if (!$standalone)` idiom used by XML-Twig.

## How

- Restored original `defaulthandle()` that always calls `cbv->dflt_sv`
- Restored `PL_sv_yes`/`PL_sv_no` for standalone in `xmlDecl()`
- Reverted POD documentation to match boolean behavior
- Updated `t/decl.t` standalone tests to verify boolean semantics
- Removed `t/char_end_doc.t` (tested the reverted behavior)

## Testing

XML-Parser: 47/47 test files pass (443 tests)

- **XML-Twig 3.54**: 4975/4978 pass (3 pre-existing failures unrelated to these changes)
- **XML-DOM 1.46**: 129/129 pass

author: phpstan-bot
body:
## Summary
PHPStan incorrectly reported `Strict comparison using === between mixed and array{NAN} will always evaluate to false` when a variable of type `mixed` was compared against multiple class constants containing `[NAN]`. After the first `=== CONST_A` check, PHPStan narrowed the type by subtracting `array{NAN}`, causing subsequent comparisons against other `[NAN]` constants to be flagged as always false.

## Changes
- Overrode `getFiniteTypes()` in `src/Type/Constant/ConstantFloatType.php` to return `[]` for NAN values
- Added regression test in `tests/PHPStan/Rules/Comparison/data/bug-11054.php`
- Added test method `testBug11054` in `tests/PHPStan/Rules/Comparison/StrictComparisonOfDifferentTypesRuleTest.php`

## Root cause
`ConstantFloatType(NAN)` inherited `getFiniteTypes()` from `ConstantScalarTypeTrait` which returned `[$this]`. This caused `ConstantArrayType` containing NAN to also report a single finite type. The `TypeSpecifier` uses `getFiniteTypes()` to decide whether to narrow (subtract) a type in the false branch of `===` checks. For NAN-containing arrays, this narrowing is incorrect because in PHP, two references to the same `[NAN]` array (e.g., class constants) ARE identical via `===` (same zval), even though structurally different `[NAN]` arrays are not. By returning `[]` from `getFiniteTypes()` for NAN, the false-branch narrowing is skipped, while the true-branch narrowing still works via the `isConstantValue()` fallback path.

## Test
The regression test verifies that comparing a `mixed` parameter against multiple class constants containing `[NAN]` produces no false-positive "always false" errors.

Fixes phpstan/phpstan#11054

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce a dedicated Audit module with backend and frontend support, implement a cross-tenant PlatformJob infrastructure for recurring jobs, enhance identity and admin UI usability, and address several stability and integration bugs.

New Features:
- Add a standalone Audit module with APIs, storage, and admin UI for viewing logs, inspecting changes, and managing per-tenant audit settings.
- Introduce permission-resolved sidebar navigation and a new Audit section with role-based access to logs and settings.
- Enable role-to-user management from the role detail page, including listing, adding, and removing assigned users.
- Expose platform APIs and UI for listing registered modules and installing them per tenant, using server-discovered module metadata.

Bug Fixes:
- Fix Keycloak user enable/disable operations by fetching and updating full user representations to satisfy Keycloak API requirements.
- Ensure last login timestamps are updated reliably on /me calls to avoid connection pool issues.
- Relax API envelope unwrapping to tolerate null data for void responses, preventing client errors on successful but body-less requests.
- Correct Dapr cache behavior for value types by using GetStateAndETagAsync so missing keys are distinguishable from falsy values.

- Load tenant-installable modules dynamically from a backend-registered module list, showing translated names and versions in the UI.
- Improve EF Core multi-tenancy by introducing a tenant-aware model cache key factory to avoid schema leakage between tenants.

Documentation:

## Proposed commit message

Replace Clone()+DeepUpdate() with single-pass DeepCopyUpdate() in add_fields, cloud/host/observer metadata, processing setup, and heartbeat eventext. DeepCopyUpdate creates fresh nested maps during merge instead of cloning the entire source first.

- **add_fields**: Detect single-key wrapper shape at init, use DeepCopyUpdate on inner map only. Split @metadata handling to bypass event.deepUpdate overhead.
- **add_cloud_metadata**: Per-value deep copy instead of full metadata.Clone(). Immutable values returned as-is.
- **add_host_metadata**: Lock-free cache read via atomic timestamp + mapstr.Pointer. DeepCopyUpdate for merge.
- **add_observer_metadata, publisher/processing (3 sites), heartbeat/eventext**: Clone()+DeepUpdate() → DeepCopyUpdate().

|-----------|---------|--------|-------------|
| add_fields (3-processor chain) | -47% | -29% | -29% |

E2E filebeat (benchmark input → mock ES, GOMAXPROCS=2, 30s): **+15.8% EPS** with 6× add_fields.

## Summary

**Root cause:** `ProfileController::update()` called `$request->user()->markAsVerified()` on line 41, but this method does not exist on the `User` model. The correct Laravel method is `markEmailAsVerified()` (from `MustVerifyEmail`), but even that would be logically wrong here — the controller intentionally clears `email_verified_at` when the email changes (lines 35-36), so re-verifying immediately after would negate that logic.

**Fix applied:** Removed the erroneous `markAsVerified()` call entirely. The profile update flow now correctly:
1. Fills validated data
2. Clears `email_verified_at` if the email changed
3. Saves and redirects

**Files changed:**
- `app/Http/Controllers/Settings/ProfileController.php` — removed the undefined `markAsVerified()` call

Existing tests in `tests/Feature/Settings/ProfileUpdateTest.php` already cover both scenarios (email changed → verification cleared, email unchanged → verification preserved).

author: sudrao88
body:
## Summary

- **Stream-process sync downloads** instead of buffering all files before processing — cards now render incrementally as each file arrives from Google Drive
- **Defer attachment loading** — cards appear immediately with textual info (title, enrichment, tags) while images/PDFs show a loading placeholder, then populate once the download phase completes
- **Replace expensive full-IDB reload** with targeted `upsertMemory` state updates that insert/update individual cards without re-reading the entire database

## Details

### Problem
During sync, cards would not appear until *all* files finished downloading (up to 50 concurrent). Users had to wait for the entire sync to complete before seeing any content. Large attachment files (images, PDFs embedded as base64) further delayed rendering.

### Solution

**`downloadFilesStreaming`** (new, `googleDriveService.ts`) — Producer-consumer pattern:
- 50 download workers run fully in parallel (same `DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY` as before)
- A single processing loop drains items sequentially as downloads complete
- Eliminates race conditions on shared arrays while keeping full download throughput

**`onMemorySynced` callback** (new, `SyncContext.tsx`) — Fires after each memory is saved to IndexedDB:
- For memories with attachments: emits a lightweight version first (`_attachmentsDeferred: true`, attachment metadata without data), then the full version after the download phase
- For text-only memories: emits immediately with full data

**`upsertMemory`** (new, `useMemories.ts`) — Efficient incremental state update:
- Inserts new cards in sorted position (descending timestamp)
- Updates existing cards in-place with change detection to avoid unnecessary re-renders
- Replaces the debounced `refreshMemories()` approach that reloaded all memories from IDB

**MemoryCard attachment placeholders** — Shows spinner for images and "loading..." for documents when `_attachmentsDeferred` is true.

### Coverage
- Works for both **delta sync** and **force full sync** (both flow through `doDeltaSync → executeSyncPlan`)
- All 232 existing tests pass with updated mocks

## Test plan

- [ ] Sync with 10+ memories on a second device — verify cards appear one by one during sync, not all at once after sync completes
- [ ] Sync memories with image/PDF attachments — verify card text appears immediately with loading placeholder, then attachments populate
- [ ] Verify no UI flickering during sync (cards don't jump or flash)
- [ ] Verify pinned memories remain at top during incremental sync
- [ ] Force full sync from settings — verify same incremental behavior
- [ ] Verify periodic background sync still works correctly
- [ ] Run `npx vitest run` — all 232 tests pass

author: markus-lassfolk
body:
Fixes #76. Adds --occurrence, --instance, and --scope flags to delete-event.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Medium risk because it changes calendar deletion/cancellation behavior and introduces new EWS request shapes (`OccurrenceItemId`) that could affect which items get removed or how cancellations are sent.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds support for deleting/cancelling *individual occurrences* of recurring calendar events via new `delete-event` flags: `--occurrence` (instance index), `--instance` (date lookup), and `--scope` (with `future` explicitly rejected and `all` mapping to master deletion).
> 
> Extends the EWS client to fetch recurrence metadata (`CalendarItemType`, `RecurringMasterItemId`) and updates `deleteEvent`/`cancelEvent` to target occurrences using `OccurrenceItemId`; for occurrence cancellations, it skips `CancelCalendarItem` and uses `DeleteItem` with meeting cancellations instead.

body:
## Description

This pull request introduces new configuration options for raid checks, improves gem and meta gem validation, adds a manual sync command for Loot Helper data, and enhances the clarity of raid check outputs with class-colored player names. The changes are primarily focused on improving loot profile flexibility, making raid preparation checks more robust, and providing better tools for guild coordination.

**Raid Check Configuration Enhancements:**

* Added two new raid check options to loot profiles: `checkGemsInSockets` (enables/disables gem socket validation) and `requireMetaGem` (enforces the presence of a meta gem). These options are now included in profile creation, copying, export/import, and can be toggled via new setter methods. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dab0a721228bc951427760a7f6fcf2d9551fbb22fdb0b176b2251ef735e9e4c1R45-R55) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-dab0a721228bc951427760a7f6fcf2d9551fbb22fdb0b176b2251ef735e9e4c1R94-R95) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-dab0a721228bc951427760a7f6fcf2d9551fbb22fdb0b176b2251ef735e9e4c1R485-R486) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-dab0a721228bc951427760a7f6fcf2d9551fbb22fdb0b176b2251ef735e9e4c1R547-R574) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-dab0a721228bc951427760a7f6fcf2d9551fbb22fdb0b176b2251ef735e9e4c1R1200-R1205) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-b1ef62798af8b1bbf07b3b1f232a2a80f0859b35e99d682061f607f33de78509L4-R4)

**Raid Check Logic Improvements:**

* The raid check now validates gem sockets only if `checkGemsInSockets` is enabled, and enforces meta gem presence if `requireMetaGem` is enabled. Added robust detection for meta gems (by quality and color) and improved handling for gem checks. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c1a74d260692f0fac85b96a9c76ccc2c0f0af93979d3d8c28ccfc8b22c0c7703R135-R176) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c1a74d260692f0fac85b96a9c76ccc2c0f0af93979d3d8c28ccfc8b22c0c7703L221-R292) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c1a74d260692f0fac85b96a9c76ccc2c0f0af93979d3d8c28ccfc8b22c0c7703R312-R315)
* Player names in raid check outputs are now colorized by class for improved readability, using new utility functions. All summary and warning messages reflect this enhancement. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c1a74d260692f0fac85b96a9c76ccc2c0f0af93979d3d8c28ccfc8b22c0c7703R46-R72) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c1a74d260692f0fac85b96a9c76ccc2c0f0af93979d3d8c28ccfc8b22c0c7703R414-R419) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c1a74d260692f0fac85b96a9c76ccc2c0f0af93979d3d8c28ccfc8b22c0c7703R436) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-c1a74d260692f0fac85b96a9c76ccc2c0f0af93979d3d8c28ccfc8b22c0c7703L370-R448) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-c1a74d260692f0fac85b96a9c76ccc2c0f0af93979d3d8c28ccfc8b22c0c7703L426-R504) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-c1a74d260692f0fac85b96a9c76ccc2c0f0af93979d3d8c28ccfc8b22c0c7703L464-R542)

**Loot Helper Sync Improvements:**

* Added a new public API method `RequestManualSync` to trigger a manual sync check with the session coordinator, only requesting missing profile or log data if necessary.
* Added `/sf loot sync` slash command for users to manually request a sync, with clear user feedback for all possible outcomes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-cbd109f07ce085950e885af0f03ec83a22911c5a08f3a2636e3cb729c06fdd31R116-R149) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cbd109f07ce085950e885af0f03ec83a22911c5a08f3a2636e3cb729c06fdd31R333-R337) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-cbd109f07ce085950e885af0f03ec83a22911c5a08f3a2636e3cb729c06fdd31L400-R439)

author: s3cr1z
body:
### 🎯 What:
Fixed a security vulnerability where user passwords were stored in plaintext using `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage`.

### ⚠️ Risk:
`AsyncStorage` is not an encrypted storage solution. On some platforms (especially older Android versions), its content could be accessed by other applications or through device backups, potentially exposing the user's password.

### 🛡️ Solution:
Replaced `AsyncStorage` with `expo-secure-store` for password-related operations. `expo-secure-store` provides a way to encrypt and securely store key-value pairs locally on the device.

**Key Implementation Details:**
- **Secure Storage:** Used `SecureStore.setItemAsync`, `SecureStore.getItemAsync`, and `SecureStore.deleteItemAsync` for managing the user password.
- **Migration:** Added logic in `loadAuthState` to detect if a password exists in the legacy `AsyncStorage`. If found, it's moved to `SecureStore` and immediately deleted from `AsyncStorage` to ensure a seamless and secure transition for existing users.
- **Logout Cleanup:** Updated the `logout` function to explicitly delete the password from `SecureStore`.

body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the remaining altloc handling gaps in the standard-residue hydrogen workflow.

- preserve `label_alt_id` for added hydrogens in the mmCIF preserve-write path
- make mover generation conformer-aware so altloc A/B sidechains produce separate movers
- add regression tests for altloc-aware mover generation and writer output

## Root Cause

Hydrogen placement had already become conformer-aware, but two downstream stages still collapsed that information:

- `writeWithDocument()` always wrote `.` for added H `label_alt_id`
- `generateMovers()` grouped atoms only by residue/name and ignored altloc, so A/B conformers were merged into one optimization problem

## Impact

- added hydrogens now keep their conformer assignment in output mmCIF
- altloc sidechains now get independent methyl/flip mover grouping instead of being mixed together
- the altloc placement pipeline is now consistent across placement, optimization, and serialization

## Validation

- `zig test src/root.zig`
- `zig build run -- src/test_data/ala_altloc.cif --json /tmp/zreduce_altloc.json -o /tmp/zreduce_altloc_out.cif`

The manual altloc check now shows two methyl movers and added hydrogens written with `label_alt_id` `A` and `B`.

author: s243a
body:
## Summary

Fix the Go composable transitive closure template that produced invalid Go code with "non-declaration statement outside function body" syntax errors.

## Root Cause

The composable template system concatenates: `tc_definitions + tc_input_stdin + tc_interface_cli`

Two problems:
1. `tc_input_stdin.mustache` contained bare `for scanner.Scan() { ... }` code that ended up between the `Check()` function closing brace and the `func main()` declaration — outside any function body
2. `tc_interface_cli.mustache` used `{{> tc_input_stdin}}` Mustache partial syntax, but the composable system concatenates rendered templates — it doesn't resolve partials, so the partial reference was rendered literally

## Fix

- **`tc_input_stdin.mustache`**: Made empty (the stdin code is now part of the CLI interface)
- **`tc_interface_cli.mustache`**: Contains the full `func main()` with stdin reading inline, argument parsing, and BFS query dispatch

This matches how the composable system works: `definitions + (empty) + cli` = valid Go program.

## Runtime Validation

| Query | Before | After |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `ancestor(a,d)` via a→b→c→d | Build error | `a:d` exit 0 |
| `ancestor(d,a)` | Build error | exit 1 |
| Monolithic path | Already worked | Still works |

## Test plan

- [x] All 115 JVM assembly tests pass
- [x] All 95 WAT tests pass
- [x] Go composable TC compiles and runs correctly
- [x] Go monolithic TC still works
- [x] Both positive and negative reachability queries correct

author: tagar
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

Add path traversal validation in `NettyStreamManager.openStream()` for the directory streaming branch. The resolved file path is canonicalized and verified to stay within the registered directory before serving.

### Why are the changes needed?

`NettyStreamManager.openStream()` constructs file paths from user-supplied stream IDs without validating that the resolved path stays within the registered directory. When stream type is a registered directory, `fname` (from the URL path) is passed directly to `new File(dir, fname)`. A crafted `StreamRequest` with `streamId` containing `../` sequences (e.g., `/classes/../../etc/passwd`) can read arbitrary files accessible to the Spark process.

The attack vector:
1. `StreamRequest.streamId` arrives from the network with no sanitization
2. `TransportRequestHandler.processStreamRequest()` passes it directly to `streamManager.openStream()`
3. `openStream()` splits on `/` and for directory types does `new File(dir, fname)` — `fname` can contain `../`
4. When `spark.authenticate=false` (the default), no auth is required, so any network-reachable client can exploit this

The `"files"` and `"jars"` branches are not affected — they use `ConcurrentHashMap.get()` key lookups, not path construction.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Only malicious requests containing path traversal sequences are rejected. Legitimate directory streaming is unaffected.

### How was this patch tested?

Existing `NettyRpcEnvSuite` (41 tests) passes — includes directory file serving tests that exercise the patched code path.

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?

Yes — co-authored with Claude Code (Anthropic).

### Motivation

- Ensure backfill inserts have valid primary key components and no duplicate rows, and make `raw_json` safe for JSON storage by converting `Timestamp`/`datetime` values. 
- Avoid writing entirely empty frames or rows with missing required columns that would cause DB errors or collisions. 

### Description

- Added `PRIMARY_KEY_COLS` and helper functions ` _fill_missing_key_parts` and `_prepare_rows` to infer missing `market`/`asset` parts, normalize `ts` to UTC datetimes, drop rows missing `ts`/`protocol`, and remove duplicates by the primary key. 
- Updated `write_rows` to use the prepared/cleaned DataFrame and convert `pd.Timestamp` values to Python datetimes before merging into the DB. 
- Changed the main fetch flow to filter out empty frames with `non_empty_frames = [f for f in frames if not f.empty and not f.dropna(how='all').empty]` and only concatenate non-empty frames. 
- In `pipelines/normalize.py` added `_to_json_safe` to recursively convert `pd.Timestamp`, `datetime`, lists, and dicts into JSON-safe values and use it when populating `raw_json`.

## Summary

Refactor the monolithic `PromotionForm` component in the admin app to improve maintainability, readability, and type safety.

## Details

- **Modularization**: Decomposed the large `PromotionForm.tsx` into smaller sub-components:
  - `PromotionBasicInfo`: Handles basic metadata like active status and dates.
  - `PromotionImages`: Manages image uploads for PC/Mobile banners and thumbnails.
  - `PromotionLanguages`: Handles multi-language tabs and text fields.
- **Logic Extraction**: Moved all form state management, validation logic, and image upload handlers into a new `usePromotionForm` custom hook.
- **Type Safety**: Implemented discriminated unions for the `mode` prop ("add" | "edit") to ensure type-safe submission payloads and correct API field mapping.
- **Error Handling**: Added validation and automatic redirection in `EditPage.tsx` to handle invalid promotion IDs or data fetch failures.
- **Context API**: Utilized `FormProvider` from `react-hook-form` to simplify data flow and reduce prop drilling.

## Notes

- This refactor maintains the existing UI and functionality while significantly cleaning up the codebase.
- Verified with `tsc` and `eslint` to ensure no regressions or linting issues.

author: shyn
body: 💡 What: Changed the return type of `SessionManager.RebuildContext()` from `IReadOnlyList` directly to `List`, and removed the downstream `.ToList()` calls in `AgentSession.cs`. 🎯 Why: `SessionManager.RebuildContext()` returns a freshly allocated list for the reconstructed conversation history. Because `AgentSession` needs to mutate this list by appending further messages (e.g. extension messages, tool execution messages, errors), it previously called `.ToList()` on the returned `IReadOnlyList`. This caused an unnecessary O(N) allocation and element copy on every generation loop (both in `PromptAsync` and `ContinueAsync`). By surfacing the concrete `List` directly, we transfer ownership to the caller, preventing the redundant allocation. 📊 Impact: Reduces array allocations and copies per loop iteration. In highly compacting conversations where token counts are large, avoiding a copy of the message list array alleviates garbage collection pressure on the hot path. 🔬 Measurement: Run a simple profiler on `AgentSession.PromptAsync` to observe the absence of `.ToList()` allocations against the number of `LlmMessage` entries. Run the unit tests (`dotnet test`) to verify regressions have not been introduced. Recorded learning in `.jules/bolt.md`. --- *PR created automatically by Jules for task [17184923061034374107](https://jules.google.com/task/17184923061034374107) started by @shyn* ---

## Summary
Introduces a new "CAML Article Writer" corpus action template that automatically generates polished CAML (Corpus Article Markup Language) articles for corpus home pages. This template researches document collections and produces narrative-driven articles combining prose with rich data visualizations.

## Key Changes

- **Added comprehensive CAML syntax reference and editorial guidelines** (`_CAML_ARTICLE_SYSTEM_INSTRUCTIONS`):
  - Complete CAML language specification covering frontmatter, chapters, and block types (cards, pills, tabs, timeline, map, case-history, etc.)

body:
### Motivation
- Improve host metrics ingestion and operational workflows by supporting agent tokens, automatic device creation from agent metrics, and host registration by IP. 
- Provide per-host alert override schema and admin controls for alert settings, plus an SMTP helper for outbound alerts. 
- Enhance floor-plan and map UX with richer canvas tools, PDF background rendering, export improvements, per-map tooltip settings, persistent node positions, and group-box styling.

### Description
- Metrics and agent features: added token validation and lifecycle (`agent_tokens`) with `ensureAgentTokenTable`, secure token generation (`generateAgentToken`), device auto-creation from host metrics (`createDeviceForHost`), host registration endpoints (`register_host_ip`, `create_device_from_host`), and migration helpers for host alerts (`ensureHostOverrideSchema`); integrated alert checks on metric submission.  
- Host alerts and settings: new endpoints for `get_alert_settings` / `save_alert_settings` and CRUD for host alert overrides (`get_host_override`, `save_host_override`, `delete_host_override`, `export/import_host_overrides`), plus UI hooks in `host_metrics.php` to register hosts and quickly add host devices.  
- Floor-plan canvas and UI: major JS improvements in `floor-plan-canvas.js` adding symbol templates, cable preview, PDF background rendering (via `pdfjsLib`), robust SVG/PNG/PDF export using `renderToCanvas`, optimistic placement updates, and export bounds trimming; `floor_plan.php` includes UI for symbols and loads `pdfjs`/`jsPDF`.  
- Map and UX enhancements: CSS fixes for responsive layout and map height, per-map tooltip field settings and persistence (`MapApp.utils.getCurrentTooltipFields`, localStorage keys), per-user node position persistence and view snapshot (`MapApp.network` helpers), group box styling/resizing and box settings dialogs, extended icon mappings, and improved placement/copy flows.  
- API and server: wired new metrics/agent/license/host endpoints into `api.php`, tightened map update validation (`offline_delay_seconds` range and `public_view_enabled` boolean handling), added `smtp_mailer.php` helper for raw SMTP sending, and small DB/column compatibility helpers for legacy installs.

### Testing
- Ran PHP syntax checks with `php -l` across modified PHP files which reported no syntax errors.  
- Executed automated smoke tests (scripted `curl` requests) against the new metrics endpoints to verify `submit_metrics`, `get_agent_tokens`, and `create_agent_token` return JSON responses and expected HTTP status codes.

The "Indian gum" you are describing is almost certainly the pith (the soft, spongy center) found inside the dried stalks of certain plants, most commonly Wild Mustard or Gumweed.
It is not radioactive. It is a natural plant material that has been a part of "country kid" lore and indigenous tradition for a long time. 
Why is it called "Indian Gum"?
The Texture: When these plants dry out in the summer, the center of the stalk becomes a "fluffy," foamy, or pithy white material.
The Tradition: It earned the name because various Native American tribes were known to use the resins and piths of local plants as a natural chewing gum to quench thirst or freshen breath.
The Experience: If you break open a dried mustard stalk, you can pull out this white "marrow." When you first chew it, it has a slightly styrofoam-like crunch and then becomes a tasteless, chewy wad. 
Common Plants with "Indian Gum" Pith:
Wild Mustard (Brassica species): After the plant dies and dries into a "chalky white skeleton," the main stalk contains a foamy, chewy dried pith.
Gumweed (Grindelia species): These plants are naturally sticky and resinous. Native Americans used the gummy secretions on the flower heads and leaves to treat respiratory issues or as a substitute for chewing gum.
Spruce and Pine: While not "fluffy" inside a stick, the resins from these trees were the most common natural gums used by tribes in the Northeast and Plains. 
Is it Safe?
While the pith of common wild mustard is generally considered non-toxic and has no significant radioactivity, it is not recommended to chew random plant stalks today. Many plants look similar, and some—like Hemlock—are extremely poisonous. Additionally, some plants like Gumweed can accumulate selenium from the soil, which can be toxic in large amounts.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a self-contained FastAPI-based ops toolset with env-based Basic auth, background task handling, and multiple integration modules to support file, terminal and FTP workflows.
- Deliver Milestones 2–5 in the project plan by adding ZLink metrics/dashboard/latest-release, File Explorer with async archive/compress, Terminal (AJAX + WebSocket) and an FTP viewer with common workflows.
- Establish project governance and discoverability by adding docs, changelog, backlog and agent guidance files and a version file.

### Description
- Added a new FastAPI application entry at `app/main.py` with Basic auth middleware and router mounts for `zlink`, `files`, `terminal`, `ftp` and task routes and static file serving, and set app version to `0.5.0`.
- Implemented ZLink module in `app/zlink.py` with SQLite persistence (`data/advocate.db`), ingestion endpoint `POST /zlink/metrics/usage`, aggregated retrieval `GET /zlink/metrics/usage`, an inline SVG dashboard `GET /zlink/dashboard`, and a `POST /zlink/latest/refresh` endpoint that fetches/releases and caches the latest asset to `static/zlink-latest.zip` plus `GET /zlink/latest`.
- Implemented File Explorer (`app/files.py`) supporting `cwd` introspection, `POST /files/chdir`, `GET /files/list`, create/rename/upload/download endpoints, and async background archive (`/files/archive`) and compress (`/files/compress`) jobs wired to a new in-process TaskManager.
- Added an in-process async `TaskManager` (`app/tasks.py`) with `TaskRecord`, threadpool execution, progress callback and task listing/get endpoints (`app/task_routes.py`).
- Added Terminal module (`app/terminal.py`) with `POST /terminal/exec` for timed commands and `WS /terminal/ws` WebSocket interactive command interface with session-local `cd` handling.
- Added FTP viewer (`app/ftp.py`) with in-memory session logins `POST /ftp/login`, remote browse `GET /ftp/browse`, upload/download endpoints, remote `archive`/`compress`/`extract` workflows, `POST /ftp/upload-extract` and `POST /ftp/archive-download`, and artifact retrieval `GET /ftp/artifact` backed by `static/ftp`.
- Added runner and bootstrap `run.py` to ensure dependencies and start the server, `requirements.txt`, `VERSION`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `README.md`, `docs/product_design_and_milestones.md`, and agent guidance files (`AGENTS.md`, `AGENT_NOTES.md`, `agents.md`).

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this rollout; dependency installation and runtime validation could not be performed in this environment due to outbound package index/proxy restrictions, so CI or local server startup was not run.
- Playwright-based UI automation was not available because Playwright is not installed in the environment, as noted in `AGENT_NOTES.md`.
