body:
**💡 What:** 
Added core ARIA accessibility features, keyboard navigation support (Enter/Space), and screen-reader-friendly labels to the dynamic Event `TabBar` component, and corrected an invalid pointer-events CSS override on `.nodrag` elements.

**🎯 Why:**
The `TabBar` previously relied solely on mouse interactions (`onClick`/`onMouseDown`) and `title` attributes, rendering it inaccessible to keyboard-only users and uninformative to screen readers. Implementing proper ARIA roles and keyboard event handlers ensures the interface is intuitive and usable for all users without causing nested interaction bugs. The CSS pointer-events fix replaces a potentially unpredictable SVG-specific override (`all`) with a standardized HTML equivalent (`auto`).

**📸 Before/After:**
*(Visual changes are limited to a focus ring on the active tab during keyboard navigation, as seen in the generated test video/screenshot).*

**♿ Accessibility:**
- Added `role="tablist"` to the scroll container.
- Added `role="tab"`, `tabIndex={0}`, and `aria-selected` to individual tabs.
- Added `onKeyDown` for keyboard activation, with proper target-checking to prevent nested-button misfires.
- Replaced non-descriptive `title` attributes with explicit `aria-label`s on icon-only close buttons (e.g., `Close Date Event tab`) and the "New tab" button.

body:
### Motivation
- The screener should query `market_scan_results_latest` directly from the frontend rather than calling the outdated `wsp-screener` edge function that enforces legacy tier1/approved filtering.
- Simplify runtime behavior by making the existing `fetchDirectFromSupabase()` the single live data source.
- Provide a safe local fallback without invoking any edge function when direct Supabase access fails.

### Description
- Updated `fetchWspScreenerData` in `src/hooks/use-wsp-screener.ts` to always use `fetchDirectFromSupabase()` as the live data path and return its evaluated stocks and sector statuses directly.
- Removed the runtime edge-function invocation and dev/prod `/api/wsp-screener` or `functions/v1/wsp-screener` fetch paths from the hook so no `invoke('wsp-screener')`/edge fetch occurs in this flow.
- Added a local fallback response using `demoStocks` (marked as `dataSource: 'fallback'`) and updated `providerStatus.runtimeDiagnostics` to reflect the direct-Supabase path when the direct query fails.
- Left `fetchDirectFromSupabase()` behavior intact: it queries `market_scan_results_latest` with `.in('pattern', ['climbing', 'base_or_climbing'])`, uses `PAGE_SIZE = 1000` with `.range()` pagination, and loops until all pages are fetched.

### Testing
- Ran lint via `npm run -s lint`, which failed in this environment due to a missing resolver package (`@eslint/js`) referenced by the repository's ESLint config.

author: radoering
body:
### Fixed

- **Fix a path traversal vulnerability in the wheel installer that could allow malicious wheel files to write files outside the intended installation directory** ([#10792](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10792)).
- Fix an issue where `git` dependencies from annotated tags could not be updated ([#10719](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10719)).
- Fix an issue where empty `VIRTUAL_ENV` or `CONDA_PREFIX` environment variables (e.g., after `conda deactivate`) would cause Poetry to incorrectly detect an active virtualenv ([#10784](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10784)).
- Fix an issue where an incomprehensible error message was printed when `.venv` was a file instead of a directory ([#10777](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10777)).
- Fix an issue where HTTP Basic Authentication credentials could be corrupted during request preparation, causing authentication failures with long tokens ([#10748](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10748)).
- Fix an issue where `poetry publish --no-interaction --build` requested user interaction ([#10769](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10769)).
- Fix an issue where `poetry init` and `poetry new` created a deprecated `project.license` format ([#10787](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10787)).

### Docs

- Clarify the differences between `poetry install` and `poetry update` ([#10713](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10713)).
- Clarify the section of fields in the `pyproject.toml` examples ([#10753](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10753)).
- Add a note about the different installation location when Python from the Microsoft Store is used ([#10759](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10759)).
- Fix the system requirements for Poetry ([#10739](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10739)).
- Fix the `poetry cache clear` example ([#10749](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10749)).
- Fix the link to `pipx` installation instructions ([#10783](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10783)).

### poetry-core ([`2.3.2`](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/releases/tag/2.3.2))

- Fix an issue where `platform_release` could not be parsed on Debian Trixie ([#930](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/pull/930)).
- Fix an issue where using `project.readme.text` in the `pyproject.toml` file resulted in broken metadata ([#914](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/pull/914)).
- Fix an issue where dependency groups were considered equal when their resolved dependencies were equal, even if the groups themselves were not ([#919](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/pull/919)).
- Fix an issue where removing a dependency from a group that included another group resulted in other dependencies being added to the included group ([#922](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/pull/922)).
- Fix an issue where PEP 735 `include-group` entries were lost when `[tool.poetry.group]` also defined `include-groups` for the same group ([#924](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/pull/924)).
- Fix an issue where the union of `<value> not in <marker>` constraints was wrongly treated as always satisfied ([#925](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/pull/925)).
- Fix an issue where a post release with a local version identifier was wrongly allowed by a `>` version constraint ([#921](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/pull/921)).
- Fix an issue where a version with the local version identifier `0` was treated as equal to the corresponding public version ([#920](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/pull/920)).
- Fix an issue where a `!= <version>` constraint wrongly disallowed pre releases and post releases of the specified version ([#929](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/pull/929)).
- Fix an issue where `in` and `not in` constraints were wrongly not allowed by specific compound constraints ([#927](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/pull/927)).

## Summary by Sourcery

Release version 2.3.3 with security, reliability, and documentation improvements, and update metadata accordingly.

Bug Fixes:
- Address a path traversal vulnerability in the wheel installer that allowed writes outside the installation directory.
- Resolve issues with updating git dependencies from annotated tags.
- Fix incorrect virtualenv detection when VIRTUAL_ENV or CONDA_PREFIX environment variables are empty.
- Improve error handling when a .venv path is a file instead of a directory.
- Prevent corruption of HTTP Basic Authentication credentials during request preparation, especially for long tokens.
- Ensure `poetry publish --no-interaction --build` runs without requesting user interaction.
- Update `poetry init` and `poetry new` to avoid generating deprecated project.license metadata.
- Update to poetry-core 2.3.2 to fix multiple issues in environment detection, metadata generation, dependency grouping, and version/marker constraint handling.

Documentation:
- Clarify differences between `poetry install` and `poetry update`.
- Improve explanations of field sections in `pyproject.toml` examples.
- Document the different installation location when using Python from the Microsoft Store.
- Correct Poetry system requirements documentation.
- Fix the `poetry cache clear` usage example.
- Update the link to `pipx` installation instructions.

Chores:
- Update changelog and version references for the 2.3.3 release.

author: rjh-mopjones
body:
Closes #356.

## Summary

- **Gateway Kafka consumer timeout**: 1000ms → 100ms — events reach the game projection 10x faster
- **Adaptor Kafka consumer timeout**: 1000ms → 100ms — cross-service cascades (fleet→nav→station) lose up to 900ms per hop
- **Frontend poll interval**: 500ms → 200ms — UI updates 2.5x more frequently
- **Stale session recovery**: after 5 consecutive poll failures (~1s), frontend auto-creates a fresh session instead of showing "Backend unavailable" forever
- **Connection banner removed entirely** — no more amber "Backend unavailable" banner or leftover error banner CSS

## Staging test results

| Suite | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Smoke | 6/6 |
| Supply chain | 6/6 |
| Performance | 11/11 |
| UX timeline | 15/15 |
| Regression | 5/5 |

## Latency (staging, measured by performance test)

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Command ack | 133ms | 173ms |
| Ship departed (visible) | 617ms | 622ms |
| Full flight | 507ms | 512ms |
| Cross-service cascade | 206ms | 206ms |
| Stock drain regularity | CV 13% | CV 18% |

Pipeline latency is unchanged (already dominated by Kafka produce/consume + YugabyteDB txn), but **display latency** is reduced by the tighter poll interval. The Kafka timeout reduction primarily benefits sustained throughput and cross-service cascade under load, where poll-wait stacking compounds.

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The `simpleeval` package allowed arbitrary function execution resulting in potential sandbox escapes or remote code injection during the evaluation of user inputs and template conditions. The previous implementation used `simple_eval()` without explicitly disabling `functions`.
🎯 Impact: An attacker could potentially achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) by crafting malicious inputs evaluated by the system.
🔧 Fix:
- Updated `requirements.txt` to require `simpleeval>=1.0.5`.
- Replaced `simple_eval(...)` with `SimpleEval(names=..., functions={}).eval(...)` in `helpers/files.py`, `helpers/vector_db.py`, and `plugins/_memory/helpers/memory.py` to prevent code execution when only evaluating variables.
- Added a security learning journal entry to `.jules/sentinel.md`.
✅ Verification: Review the implementation changes ensuring `functions={}` is present on all `SimpleEval` instances. Run unit tests to verify system functionality has not degraded.

body:
## Summary
Transformed the chat-focused interface into a home dashboard that displays daily summaries of user records (expenses, food, todos, insights) with an interactive detail view. The assistant reply is now displayed in a dedicated panel rather than a chat message stream.

## Key Changes

### UI Architecture
- Replaced chat message stream (`chatMessages`) with a scrollable home content area (`homeContent`)
- Moved assistant reply to a dedicated panel (`assistantReply`) with typing animation support
- Converted thinking/agent logs to display in a separate `thinkingArea` instead of chat messages
- Added fixed bottom input bar (`home-input-bar`) with gradient background

### Daily Summary & Records
- Added date picker (`dateInput`) to select which day's data to view
- Implemented summary grid showing totals for expenses, food, todos, and insights
- Created clickable summary items that expand to show detailed record lists
- Added `renderDetailList()` and `renderRecordItem()` functions to display records by type with proper formatting (amounts, categories, tags)
- Implemented `toggleDetail()` to manage expand/collapse state of record details

### Data Management
- Added `refreshData()` function to reload summary statistics when date changes
- Integrated `getRecordsSummary()` and `getRecordsByDate()` calls to fetch data from storage
- Updated tool call results to trigger `refreshData()` to keep summary in sync
- Simplified chat history to store only the latest user/assistant pair

### Recording & Input
- Removed chat message bubbles for recording state; now display recording status in `micHint` instead
- Simplified recording UI to show transcription in the hint area rather than creating message elements
- Removed `recordingMsgEl` and related message creation logic

### Message Handling
- Removed `addMessage()`, `addSystemMessage()`, `addErrorMessage()`, `loadHistory()`, and `typeMessage()` functions
- Replaced with direct DOM manipulation of `assistantReply` element
- Error messages now display inline in the assistant reply panel with danger styling
- Removed chat history loading on init; now only shows welcome greeting

### Thinking/Agent Logs
- Kept collapsible thinking logs but moved them to `thinkingArea` instead of chat
- Added `removeThinking()` function to clear thinking area on errors
- Updated scroll behavior to use `scrollToTop()` instead of `scrollToBottom()`

### CSS Updates
- Added `.home-page` layout with flexbox column structure
- Created `.home-content` scrollable area with webkit scrollbar styling
- Added `.assistant-reply` panel with empty state placeholder
- Styled `.summary-item--clickable` with hover/active states and active indicator
- Added `.summary-detail` section for expandable record lists
- Created `.home-input-bar` fixed positioning with safe area inset support
- Added `.recording-indicator` styling for recording status display

## Implementation Details
- Date picker defaults to today's date and triggers `refreshData()` on change
- Summary items use `data-type` attributes to identify record type (expense/food/todo/insight)
- Record rendering uses type-specific formatters with proper escaping via `escapeHtml()`
- Thinking logs maintain step counting and tool call tracking but display in dedicated area
- Assistant reply supports markdown formatting (bold, line breaks) via `formatAssistantContent()`

author: hm21
body:
Closes #2598

## Description

Overhaul upload error categorization to use structured HTTP status codes instead of fragile string matching. Production logs showed 502 Bad Gateway being misclassified as `NETWORK_ERROR` because BlossomUploadService labeled 5xx responses as "Network error:" and `_categorizeError` matched the keyword before checking status codes.

Adds a `statusCode` field to `BlossomUploadResult` and a new `BlossomUploadFailureException` so that `_categorizeError` and `_isRetriableError` can branch on the actual HTTP status code, falling back to string matching only for non-HTTP errors (DNS, timeouts, file system).

### Key changes

**`blossom_upload_service.dart`**
- Add `int? statusCode` field to `BlossomUploadResult`
- Set `statusCode` in `_parseUploadResponse` and all `DioException` handler branches
- `DioExceptionType.badResponse` now produces "Server error (code): ..." instead of "Network error:"

**`upload_manager.dart`**

body:
## What changed

This PR adds a production-ready contact form backed by a Next.js Server Action and Resend, migrates locale routing from deprecated `middleware` to `proxy` for Next.js 16, and cleans up navigation, metadata, and branding assets around those changes.

It also now includes the latest changes from `main`, including the newer blog/feed/CI updates, and resolves the merge conflicts between those changes and the contact/routing work.

## Why it changed

The project had a partially completed set of local changes that introduced a contact form and Next 16 routing updates, but there were still runtime inconsistencies:

- legacy `/main` routes were no longer aligned with the primary homepage path
- metadata routes like `/icon` and `/sitemap.xml` were being redirected by locale handling
- page titles could render with duplicated site names
- navigation was inconsistent between navbar and footer
- documentation lagged behind the actual architecture

At the same time, `main` moved forward with additional production changes. This PR now reconciles both lines of work into one mergeable branch.

## User and developer impact

- Visitors can now contact Daniel through an on-site inquiry form.
- Legacy `/main`, `/en/main`, and `/pl/main` URLs permanently redirect to locale homepages.
- Metadata routes work correctly without locale redirects.
- English navigation now consistently uses `Home` instead of `Main`.
- Local font assets and refreshed favicon/icon generation are wired into the app.
- RSS/feed, blog filtering, CI, and other recent `main` improvements remain intact.
- README now reflects the real routing and contact-form setup.

## Root cause

The branch contained a mix of feature work, migration work, and documentation updates that were individually valid but not yet fully integrated. The main issues came from a partial transition from `middleware` to `proxy`, from homepage route changes that were not propagated through all metadata and navigation paths, and from overlapping work landing independently on `main`.

## Validation

- `npm run test`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run build`
- after merging `origin/main`, re-ran validation successfully

## Conflict resolution note

- merged latest `origin/main` into `codex/contact-form-proxy-cleanup`
- kept the `proxy`-based routing migration instead of reverting to deprecated `middleware`
- kept the richer server-action contact form implementation
- preserved newer `main` additions like feed/blog/CI/analytics-related updates

author: bububuger
body:
## Summary

- Add `POST /api/v1/shutdown` HTTP endpoint that triggers graceful shutdown sequence
- `Orchestrator.initiate_shutdown/2` waits for running agent PIDs to finish their current turn (up to `turn_timeout_ms`, capped at 60s), then invokes `:init.stop/0`
- `symphony on` now writes `~/.config/symphony/instance.json` (pid, port, started_at, project_dir)
- `symphony off` prefers HTTP `POST /api/v1/shutdown` (graceful), falls back to SIGTERM
- `symphony status` reads `instance.json` and verifies PID is alive before displaying state

## Design

Shutdown sequence per Phase 5A spec:
1. HTTP endpoint receives POST → spawns shutdown goroutine (returns 202 immediately)
2. Calls `Orchestrator.initiate_shutdown/2` via GenServer call — waits for running PIDs
3. On completion (or timeout), calls `:init.stop/0`

`bin/symphony off` flow:
1. Read port from `instance.json` (default 4000)
2. `curl POST /api/v1/shutdown` — if 2xx, wait up to 35s for process to die
3. Fallback: read PID from `instance.json` or pidfile, send SIGTERM

## Test plan

- [ ] All existing tests pass (`mix test`: 400 tests, 0 failures)
- [ ] `symphony on` creates `~/.config/symphony/instance.json` with pid/port/started_at/project_dir
- [ ] `symphony status` reads instance.json and shows running state
- [ ] `symphony off` sends HTTP shutdown and waits for graceful exit
- [ ] `curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/v1/shutdown` returns 202 and shuts down process

author: xavlimsg
body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where the load balancer doesn't update when user account usage windows reset (daily/weekly limit rollover). Accounts could remain blocked or deprioritised indefinitely after their limits refresh upstream.

**Root causes fixed:**

- **`_latest_usage_is_fresh()` ignored reset boundaries** — the freshness check only compared record age against the refresh interval, so stale 100% usage data persisted even after `reset_at` had passed. Now returns `false` when the window has rolled over, forcing an immediate re-fetch.
- **`_state_from_account()` passed stale exhausted data into the balancer** — when the last recorded sample showed 100% usage but the `reset_at` was already in the past, the account was still blocked or sorted last. Now zeros out stale percentages when the window has rolled over.
- **`select_account()` didn't fully clear usage on status recovery** — `RATE_LIMITED` recovery didn't reset `used_percent`, and `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` recovery didn't reset `secondary_used_percent`, so recovered accounts were deprioritised in usage-weighted selection.
- **Added `_account_needs_post_reset_refresh()`** — forces a usage refresh when an account's persisted `reset_at` has expired but the primary usage entry still looks fresh (covers secondary-only resets).

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `app/modules/usage/updater.py` | `_latest_usage_is_fresh()` now checks `reset_at`; new `_account_needs_post_reset_refresh()` helper; `refresh_accounts()` uses it |
| `app/modules/proxy/load_balancer.py` | `_state_from_account()` zeros stale 100% data when reset_at is past |
| `app/core/balancer/logic.py` | `select_account()` resets `used_percent` and `secondary_used_percent` on status clear |
| `tests/unit/test_usage_updater.py` | Tests for freshness check with reset boundary + account refresh helper |
| `tests/unit/test_load_balancer.py` | Tests for selection recovery with full percent reset |

## Test plan

- [x] All 677 existing unit tests pass with no regressions
- [x] New tests cover: freshness check with expired reset_at, account refresh detection, selection sort priority after reset
- [ ] Manual testing with accounts that hit rate limits and wait for window rollover

author: claude
body:
The WinPE ISO build workflow was failing with exit code 1001 when ADK setup detected a newer version already installed on Windows Server 2025 runners.

## Changes

- **Handle exit 1001 in download step**: Treat exit code 1001 (newer version installed) as success, set `exit_1001=true` output flag
- **Skip install steps conditionally**: Updated install step conditions to check both pre-install detection AND exit 1001 flag
- **Add step ID**: Added `adk-download` step ID for output propagation

## Behavior

```yaml
# Before: exit 1 on code 1001
if ($proc.ExitCode -ne 0) {
    Write-Error "ADK layout download failed (exit $($proc.ExitCode))"
    exit 1
}

# After: handle 1001 gracefully
if ($proc.ExitCode -ne 0 -and $proc.ExitCode -ne 1001) {
    Write-Error "ADK layout download failed (exit $($proc.ExitCode))"
    exit 1
}
if ($proc.ExitCode -eq 1001) {
    Write-Host "::warning::ADK setup returned exit 1001 (newer version may be installed). Skipping download/install steps."
    echo "exit_1001=true" >> $env:GITHUB_OUTPUT
    exit 0
}
```

Workflow now skips install steps and proceeds to build with pre-installed ADK components when exit 1001 is encountered.

body:
The project needed a frontend that visually matches the provided clinical dashboard reference and reflects backend inference/model data in the UI. This PR replaces the placeholder upload page with a full dashboard experience integrated with existing FastAPI endpoints, and adds complete technical documentation for the combined system.

- **Frontend UI rebuilt to match reference layout/styling**
  - Replaced `frontend/index.html` MVP page with a dashboard-style interface:
    - left navigation/brand rail
    - patient/top status bar
    - X-ray viewport with inference badge + overlays
    - analysis + metrics side cards
    - diagnostic history timeline
    - report download CTA
  - Preserved single-file frontend architecture (HTML/CSS/JS) to align with current repo structure.

- **Backend-driven frontend behavior**
  - Wired UI state to backend endpoints:
    - `GET /api/health` → AI/service status badge
    - `GET /api/metrics` → architecture/status metadata rendering
    - `POST /api/predict` → primary finding + confidence + overlay text updates
  - Added no-caries overlay behavior: detection boxes are hidden when backend prediction is `No Caries`.

- **Inference/metric presentation logic refined**
  - Replaced ad hoc inline magic values with named constants in JS where appropriate.
  - Corrected F1 display calculation to use harmonic mean on ratio values.
  - Removed non-standard CSS `zoom` usage and kept responsive behavior via media-query layout changes.

- **Complete technical documentation added**
  - Introduced `README.md` with:
    - backend architecture and endpoint contract
    - frontend architecture and data flow
    - runtime/setup details
    - training/prediction script roles
    - operational requirements and extension points

Example integration path now used in the frontend:

```js
const [healthRes, metricsRes] = await Promise.all([
  fetch("/api/health"),
  fetch("/api/metrics")
]);

const response = await fetch("/api/predict", {
  method: "POST",
  body: formData
});
const data = await response.json(); // { prediction, confidence }
```

author: greenheadhq
body:
## Summary

- `run-loop.sh`에서 holdout eval이 전 iteration에서 실패할 때, `best_iteration`이 첫 iteration에 고정되던 문제를 해결한다.
- `best_train_fallback` 변수로 train score를 추적하되, test 성공이 한 번이라도 있으면 train fallback을 비활성화하여 혼합 시나리오도 안전하게 처리한다.

Closes #322

## 기존 문제/배경

PR #321에서 test eval 실패 시 graceful degradation을 도입하면서 `best_iteration == 0` fallback을 추가했다. 이 fallback은 첫 iteration에서만 트리거되어, 이후 iteration에서 train score가 개선되어도 갱신되지 않았다.

```
Iteration 1: train 8/12, test FAIL → best_iteration=1 (fallback)
Iteration 2: train 10/12, test FAIL → best_iteration=1 (변경 없음!)
Iteration 3: train 11/12, test FAIL → best_iteration=1 (변경 없음!)
→ --apply: iteration 1의 description 적용 (train 8/12)
→ 기대: iteration 3의 description 적용 (train 11/12)
```

## CIR (Change Intent Record)

- **v1** (`af5e55e`): test eval graceful degradation 도입 (`|| true` + 결과 파싱 조건부 처리)
- **v2** (`392d39e`): `best_iteration == 0` fallback 추가로 첫 iteration 최소 설정 보장 (Codex R2)
- **v3** (이번 변경): Codex R3-R5에서 3회 연속 "train score 미갱신" 지적 → 별도 이슈 #322로 분리 후 구현

**trade-off**: `best_train_fallback` 변수 1개 추가로 상태 복잡도가 미세하게 증가하지만, all-holdout-fail 시 최적 train score의 description을 선택할 수 있다.

## ADR

| 대안 | 설명 | 장점 | 단점 | 결정 |
|------|------|------|------|------|
| `best_iteration == 0` fallback 유지 | 첫 iteration만 설정 | 단순 | train score 개선 무시 | ❌ |
| `best_train_fallback` + `best_test_passed < 0` 가드 | train score 추적 + 혼합 시나리오 방어 | 최적 train description 선택, 혼합 시나리오 안전 | 변수 1개 추가 | ✅ |
| `best_test_passed` 재사용 (가드 없음) | train score를 `best_test_passed`에 직접 저장 | 변수 추가 없음 | `TEST_SCORE_AVAILABLE` 가드 오동작 | ❌ |

## 구현 상세

| 파일 | 변경 | 내용 |
|------|------|------|
| `modules/shared/programs/claude/files/scripts/run-loop.sh` | 수정 | 변수 추가 + else 블록 조건문 교체 |

### 핵심 코드

```bash
# BEFORE (run-loop.sh:355)
if (( best_iteration == 0 )); then
  best_iteration=$iteration
  cp "$work_dir/current_desc.txt" "$work_dir/best_desc.txt"
fi

# AFTER (run-loop.sh:357)
# best_test_passed < 0: test 성공이 한 번도 없을 때만 train fallback 활성화
if (( best_test_passed < 0 && train_passed > best_train_fallback )); then
  best_train_fallback=$train_passed
  best_iteration=$iteration
  cp "$work_dir/current_desc.txt" "$work_dir/best_desc.txt"
fi
```

## 참고 레퍼런스

- Issue #322 — 이 PR이 해결하는 이슈
- Issue #320 — parent issue (train/test 분리 평가 아키텍처)
- PR #321 (`392d39e`) — eval 순서 변경 + `best_iteration == 0` fallback 도입
- `75b4a25` — test_results 없는 iteration에서 — 표시 fix
- `af5e55e` — test eval graceful degradation fix
- `68127e0` — eval 순서 변경 (train → test → improve)

## Human Test Plan

### 정상 동작 검증

1. all-holdout-fail 시나리오에서 `run-loop.sh --apply`를 실행한다.
   - **기대**: 가장 높은 train score를 가진 iteration의 description이 적용된다.
   - **실패 시**: `best_train_fallback` 변수가 train_passed와 올바르게 비교되는지, `best_test_passed < 0` 가드가 활성화되는지 확인.

2. 일부 iteration에서만 test가 성공하는 혼합 시나리오에서 실행한다.
   - **기대**: test 기반 best가 유지되고 train fallback이 이를 덮어쓰지 않는다.
   - **실패 시**: `best_test_passed` 값이 0 이상으로 설정되었는지, 가드가 fallback을 비활성화하는지 확인.

### 엣지 케이스

3. holdout==0으로 실행한다.
   - **기대**: 기존 동작 유지 (train score 기반 `best_test_passed` 갱신, else 블록 미진입).
   - **실패 시**: holdout==0 경로(361-365행)가 변경되지 않았는지 확인.

## Pre-Merge E2E 테스트 가이드

### Phase 0: 정적 검증

```bash
# 1. best_train_fallback 변수 존재 확인
grep -q "best_train_fallback=-1" modules/shared/programs/claude/files/scripts/run-loop.sh
# 기대: exit 0

# 2. old fallback 패턴 부재 확인
! grep -q "best_iteration == 0" modules/shared/programs/claude/files/scripts/run-loop.sh
# 기대: exit 0

# 3. best_test_passed < 0 가드 존재 확인
grep -q "best_test_passed < 0 && train_passed > best_train_fallback" modules/shared/programs/claude/files/scripts/run-loop.sh
# 기대: exit 0
```

### Phase 1: 기능 검증

> "변경된 조건문이 올바르게 구성되었는지 확인"

```bash
# train_fallback 갱신 코드 존재 확인
grep -q "best_train_fallback=\$train_passed" modules/shared/programs/claude/files/scripts/run-loop.sh
# 기대: exit 0
```

- **기대**: train_passed 값이 best_train_fallback에 저장되는 코드가 존재한다.
- **실패 시**: else 블록(351-362행) 내부에서 `best_train_fallback=$train_passed` 할당이 있는지 확인.

### Phase 2: Regression

> "기존 경로(test 성공, holdout==0)가 변경되지 않았는지 확인"

```bash
# test 성공 경로 유지 확인
grep -q "test_passed > best_test_passed" modules/shared/programs/claude/files/scripts/run-loop.sh
# 기대: exit 0

# holdout==0 경로 유지 확인
grep -q "train_passed > best_test_passed" modules/shared/programs/claude/files/scripts/run-loop.sh
# 기대: exit 0

# TEST_SCORE_AVAILABLE 가드 유지 확인
grep -q 'best_test_passed -lt 0' modules/shared/programs/claude/files/scripts/run-loop.sh
# 기대: exit 0
```

author: pabloroman
body:
## Summary

Fixes a deflationary ability spiral where, after many seasons (10+), all top-rated players (>80) end up over 30 years old, young talent never reaches elite levels, and squads accumulate 38-40 year olds.

**Root cause:** Youth intake used `teamAvg × factor` (55-75%, capped at 70) — as team averages declined over seasons, youth got progressively weaker, creating a self-reinforcing spiral. Combined with a development curve that peaked too early (physical decline at 25, technical at 27) and a weak quality gap bonus, young players could never catch up.

**Key changes:**

- **Flatten development curve** — Technical growth extends through age 28 (was 24), physical plateau through 26 (was 22), meaningful decline delayed to 29+. Matches real football peaks (27-30)
- **Tier-based youth intake** — Replaces fragile `teamAvg × %` formula with absolute tier-based ability ranges (same pattern the academy already uses). A tier 3 team always produces tier 2 youth with potential to reach tier 4, regardless of how the average has shifted
- **8% wonderkid chance** — AI youth intake can occasionally produce exceptional prospects at the team's median tier with potential 2 tiers above
- **Stronger quality gap bonus** — Max 1.5× (was 1.3×), steeper curve, applies until age 30 (was 28)
- **Higher potential generation** — Young players get wider potential ranges, allowing youth to realistically reach 80+

## Test plan

- [x] All unit tests pass (31 passed, 0 new failures)
- [ ] Run `php artisan app:simulate-season` across 10+ seasons and verify:
  - Young players (20-25) can reach 80+ ability
  - Squad average ability stabilizes rather than declining each season
  - Players 30+ still decline, just more gradually
  - Occasional wonderkids appear in AI squads
- [ ] Spot-check age/ability distribution: top-rated players should include a healthy mix of ages, not just 30+

author: copilot
body:
`generate_attention_maps` was capturing RPN proposals by directly replacing `detector.rpn.filter_proposals` at runtime — a fragile pattern that bypasses PyTorch's module lifecycle and leaves the model in a broken state if an exception occurs mid-iteration.

## Changes

### `awada/utils/attention.py`
- Removed `original_filter_proposals` / `capturing_filter_proposals` monkey-patch
- Registered a `rpn_hook` via `detector.rpn.register_forward_hook(rpn_hook)` that stores `output[0]` (boxes) and `output[1]` (scores) into `rpn_proposals`
- Handles the stock torchvision eval-mode case where `output[1]` is an empty losses `dict` by falling back to all-ones scores
- `hook_handle.remove()` called unconditionally in `finally`

```python
def rpn_hook(module, input, output):
    boxes = output[0]
    raw_scores = output[1]
    scores = raw_scores if isinstance(raw_scores, list) else [
        torch.ones(len(b), device=b.device) for b in boxes
    ]
    rpn_proposals["boxes"] = boxes
    rpn_proposals["scores"] = scores

hook_handle = detector.rpn.register_forward_hook(rpn_hook)
try:
    ...
finally:
    hook_handle.remove()
```

### `tests/test_attention.py`
- Replaced the MagicMock `detector.rpn` (which can't fire real hooks) with a `_FakeRPN(nn.Module)` whose `forward` returns `(boxes_list, scores_list)`, exercising the hook registration path end-to-end
- `_build_detector` now calls `fake_rpn(imgs)` inside the detector's `side_effect` to trigger the hook

Instead, use PyTorch's official register_forward_hook API to attach a hook to the RPN module that captures the boxes and scores outputs into a dictionary. body:
- [x] Analyze root cause: zoom bar steals height from scroll container on mobile - [x] CSS: Changed `.prev-col` mobile `min-height` from `120px` to `50vh` - [x] CSS: Changed `.form-col` mobile `height` from `50vh` to `45vh` - [x] JSX: Moved zoom bar inside the scrollable container with `position:sticky; top:0` - [x] Code review passed with no issues - [x] Changes verified correct
Original prompt ## Fix: Mobile preview cannot scroll to see footer on smartphones ### Context On branch `copilot/revert-index-html-and-fix-bugs` (PR #2), the mobile preview still cannot scroll to see the bottom/footer of the newsletter preview. This PR should be based on that branch. ### Root Cause Analysis The layout structure on mobile (≤ 850px) is: ``` .main-wrap (flex-direction: column, 100vh) └── .form-col (height: 50vh, flex: none) └── .prev-col (flex: 1, min-height: 120px) └── Zoom bar div (flexShrink: 0, ~40px) ← takes space from .prev-col └── Scrollable div (flex: 1, overflow: auto) └── Wrapper div (794*scale × 1123*scale) └── Spacer div (height: 80) ``` The problem is that `.prev-col` gets `flex:1` with only `min-height:120px` on mobile. After the zoom bar takes ~40px, only ~80px remain for the scrollable area. The preview (even at 30% scale = ~337px tall) is much larger than 80px, so the bottom is cut off. ### Required Changes in `index.html` (on branch `copilot/revert-index-html-and-fix-bugs`) #### 1. Increase `.prev-col` min-height on mobile In the CSS `@media(max-width:850px)` block (around line 512), change: ```css /* Before */ .prev-col{flex:1;min-height:120px;padding:8px;overflow:auto} /* After */ .prev-col{flex:1;min-height:50vh;padding:8px;overflow:auto} ``` This ensures the preview column gets at least half the viewport height on mobile. #### 2. Make the zoom bar collapsible/smaller on mobile The zoom bar takes ~40px of fixed space. On mobile, reduce its size by: - Reduce padding from `6px 0` to `4px 0` - Reduce the button font sizes - Or alternatively, make the zoom bar part of the scrollable area instead of being fixed above it The better approach: **Move the zoom bar INSIDE the scrollable area** so it doesn't steal height from the scroll container. Change the structure so the zoom bar scrolls with the preview content but sticks to top using `position:sticky`. Specifically, in the JSX around line 676-693, restructure from: ```jsx {/* Current: zoom bar OUTSIDE scroll area */}
{/* zoom bar */} ...
{/* scrollable */}
``` Change to: ```jsx {/* Fixed: zoom bar INSIDE scroll area with sticky positioning */}
{/* zoom buttons unchanged */}
``` This way: - The zoom bar uses `position:sticky; top:0` so it stays visible at the top while scrolling - The entire `.prev-col` space is available for scrolling - No height is "stolen" by a fixed-position zoom bar - The footer of the preview is reachable by scrolling #### 3. Also change `.form-col` mobile height from 50vh to `min-height:40vh` with flex On very small screens, 50vh for the form is too much. Change to: ```css .form-col{width:100%;min-width:unset;max-width:unset;flex:none;height:45vh;border-right:none} ``` ### Summary of changes: 1. CSS: `.prev-col` mobile `min-height: 50vh` instead of `120px` 2. CSS: `.form-col` mobile `height: 45vh` instead of `50vh` 3. JSX: Move zoom bar inside the scrollable container with `position:sticky; top:0` so it doesn't steal scroll space 4. ### Motivation

- Upgrade the static dashboard to a more opinionated and testable decision engine with clearer country/location modeling and comparison options.
- Improve signal coverage by adding live job and market feeds so recommendations can react to current opportunities and market momentum.
- Make state handling and UI rendering more robust and maintainable by normalizing weights, caching DOM nodes, and persisting engine snapshots.

- Bumped local state version (`STORAGE_KEY` → `...-v2`), introduced `COUNTRY_LIBRARY`, `comparisonCountryIds`, and `hydrateState` to centralize and normalize persisted defaults and optional comparison countries.

- UI and rendering refactor: cache DOM nodes in `E` via `cacheElements`, consolidate many `render*` helpers, add an "Opportunity Radar" section and a "What changed" change-tracking view (`computeChanges`), wire comparison country selects, import/export/reset behavior via `hydrateState`, and update `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `README.md` to match feature changes.

## ⚠️ DO NOT REVIEW — CI PERFORMANCE TEST RUN ⚠️

This PR exists **solely to measure CI timing impact** of sccache compiler caching.

**Will be closed after timing data is collected. Not a real PR.**

## Summary

- Adds [`mozilla-actions/sccache-action`](https://github.com/mozilla-actions/sccache-action) to all compilation-heavy CI workflows
- sccache caches individual **rustc compilation units** using the GitHub Actions cache backend
- Unlike cargo target-dir caching (keyed by commit SHA), sccache provides **cross-commit cache reuse** — only recompiling changed crates
- Research shows **11-35% build speedup** with warm sccache cache

## Workflows modified

| Workflow | Jobs affected |
|----------|--------------|
| `create-cache.yml` | nextest-archive (test binary compilation) |
| `clippy.yml` | clippy_check |
| `constants-check.yml` | check-consts |
| `cargo-hack-check.yml` | native-targets, wasm-targets, fuzz-targets |

## Expected impact

- **Cold cache (first run)**: ~5% overhead from sccache startup + cache population
- **Warm cache (subsequent runs)**: **11-35% faster** compilation across all affected jobs
- Biggest wins on iterative PRs where only a few crates change between pushes

# Pull Request

## Description

`onload()` blocks Obsidian startup by awaiting `initializeApiClient()` and `checkFirstRun()`, both of which spawn external CLI processes — 1Password CLI (`op`) for token resolution (up to 3 sequential spawns) and Copilot CLI for auth validation (30s timeout). });

## Summary
- Wraps the proactive follow-up pass in `RunAsync` with a try/catch so failures don't discard the already-completed response
- On failure, logs the error and returns `result.Response` — the user gets their answer instead of an error message

## Problem
The follow-up pass runs after the main request is complete to look for proactive next steps. If it timed out or hit a content filter, the exception propagated all the way up to `UserMessageHandler`, which showed the user an error — even though their actual question had already been fully answered.

### Motivation
- Provide a direct file-based entry from the Template Manager to edit template files without a full visual editor. 
- Ensure only allowed template files can be opened/modified by reusing existing safety checks and services. 
- Surface a simple editor UI that warns about rendering impact and supports creating missing templates safely. 

### Description
- Added `GET /admin/templates/edit` and `POST /admin/templates/edit` routes and wired them to new `TemplateAdminController::edit` and `::update` handlers which validate paths and coordinate reads/writes. 
- Implemented editor flow in `TemplateAdminController` using `TemplateResolver`, `EditableFileRegistry`, and `DevFileService` for path validation, content loading, size limits, safe write/create, and logging via existing dev-mode logging. 
- Created an admin view `templates/admin/templates/edit.php` that uses the admin shell/card/form layout and includes: template name, template path, file editor textarea, `Save`/`Cancel` buttons, a warning badge, and a “Create template file” option when missing. 
- Added `safeCreateFile()` to `DevFileService` for atomic creation of new files inside allowed directories and updated `ControllerFactory` to inject `SessionManager`, `EditableFileRegistry`, `DevFileService`, and `LoggerInterface` into the template admin controller; changed Template Manager rows to link to `/admin/templates/edit?path=...`.

body:
## 🛠️ 설명 (Description)

마이페이지의 나의 모임, 나의 리뷰(작성 가능 한 리뷰, 작성 한 리뷰), 내가 만든 모임 목록 무한 스크롤 구현 및 찜 추가 및 해제 기능 추가 

## 📄 설계 문서 (Design Document)

관련 설계 문서나 위키 페이지가 있다면 링크를 추가해주세요.(하위 항목 노션링크 첨부)

## 📝 변경 사항 요약 (Summary)

- type.ts를 한꺼번에 관리하기 위해 `features/mypage/types.ts` 에서 관리하도록 변경
- features 내 폴더구조 변경 (components 안에 서비스 관련 항목은 상위 폴더로 변경)
- 마이페이지 목록에서 사용할 스켈레톤 및 로딩 UI 추가
- 참여한 모임 / 작성 가능한 리뷰 / 작성한 리뷰 / 내가 만든 모임 목록 API 연결
- `route.ts` 엔드포인트 추가
  - `/api/meetings/joined`
  - `/api/meetings/my`
  - `/api/users/me/reviews`
  - `/api/meetings/[meetingId]/favorites`
- route handler 중복 코드 최소화를 위해 유틸함수(`parseJsonSafely`, `nextJsonResponse`)추가
- 마이페이지 목록 무한스크롤 적용
- 모임 찜 추가/해제 훅(`useMeetingFavorite`) 추가 및 낙관적 업데이트 적용

## 💁 변경 사항 이유 (Why)

1.  타입을 서로 import 하는 경우가 많기 때문에 경로 늘어짐 방지와 중복을 최소화 하기 위해 하나의 파일에서 관리하도록 변경 
2. components 내에는 ui 관련만 최대한 남기기위해 분리
3. 로딩 시 빈화면이 아닌 어떠한 동작이 진행되고 있다는 것을 알리기위해 스켈레톤 UI 추가
4. 마이페이지 목록 API 연결
    - 참여한 모임 목록과 작성 가능한 리뷰 목록 조회 연결
    - 작성한 리뷰 목록 조회 연결
    - 내가 만든 모임 목록 조회 연결
    - 응답 데이터는 mapper를 통해 컴포넌트가 필요한 형태로 변환하도록 정리
5. route.ts 작성시 코드 중복이 많아 유틸함수로 사용할 수 있는 부분을 분리하여 코드 최소화 
6. 무한 스크롤 적용
    - `useIntersectionObserver` 훅을 활용해 마이페이지 목록 탭에 infinite query 연결
    - 커서 기반 페이지네이션(`nextCursor`, `hasMore`) 처리
    - suspanse 처리를 위해 useSuspenseInfiniteQuery 적용
    - 단 SSR 환경에서 실행될 가능성을 고려하여 dynamic import 로 방지
7. 찜하기 기능 추가
    - 찜 추가/삭제 API 연결
    - `useMeetingFavorite` 훅에서 낙관적 업데이트와 롤백 처리
8. 로딩 / 빈 상태 UI
    - DetailCard / ReviewCard 스켈레톤 추가
    - 목록 로딩 컴포넌트 추가
    - Empty 상태 UI 연결

author: copilot
body:
This PR introduces a ClickHouse schema for NVD CVE JSON 2.0 data and wires it into container startup so the database is initialized automatically on first run. It also adds CI-level validation to ensure the schema exists and supports basic analytical queries on empty tables, and cleans up workflow organization so checks are separated by concern.

- **Schema initialization for CVE analytics**
  - Added `clickhouse/init/001_create_cve_schema.sql`.
  - Creates `nvd.cve_records` with coverage for key NVD fields:
    - CVE identity/status/timestamps
    - localized descriptions
    - CVSS v2/v3.0/v3.1 metric arrays
    - weaknesses, configurations/CPE matches, references
    - CISA enrichment + evaluator fields
  - Uses `ReplacingMergeTree(updated_at)` with time partitioning and analytical sort key.

- **Compose bootstrap integration**
  - Updated `docker-compose.yml` to mount init SQL into ClickHouse entrypoint init directory:
    - `./clickhouse/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro`
  - Ensures schema is created automatically when ClickHouse starts with a fresh volume.

- **CI verification for schema presence and queryability**
  - Added checks to assert:
    - `nvd.cve_records` exists
    - empty-table count query runs
    - representative nested/array columns are queryable via `toTypeName(...)`
  - Hardened table-existence check output parsing with tab-separated format + strict grep match.

- **Workflow cleanup**
  - Kept `.github/workflows/conventional-commits.yml` focused only on commit message validation.
  - Moved compose stack + schema verification into a dedicated workflow:
    - `.github/workflows/validate-compose-stack.yml`

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml
services:
  clickhouse:
    volumes:
      - clickhouse-data:/var/lib/clickhouse
      - ./clickhouse/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
```

```sql
-- clickhouse/init/001_create_cve_schema.sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS nvd.cve_records
(
  cve_id String,
  source_identifier LowCardinality(String),
  ...
)
ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(updated_at)
PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(published)
ORDER BY (published, cve_id);
```

## Summary

- Convert all `arf ipc` subcommands to output structured JSON (pretty-printed on terminal, compact when piped)
  - `list`: text table → `{"sessions": [...]}`
  - `eval`: mixed stdout/stderr → `{"stdout", "stderr", "value", "error"}`
  - `send`/`shutdown`: text messages → `{"accepted": true}`
  - `session`/`history`: unchanged (already JSON)
- Fixed JSON schema: all fields are always present (`null` when not applicable), no field omission
- Remove `arf ipc status` subcommand (superseded by `session`)
- Add structured JSON error output to stderr with string error codes (`R_BUSY`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `TRANSPORT_ERROR`, etc.) and actionable `hint` field
- Error JSON always includes all fields: `code`, `message`, `hint`, `data` (null when not applicable)
- `USER_IS_TYPING` error includes editor buffer in `error.data.buffer` for AI agent awareness
- R evaluation errors now exit 0 with error in JSON response (distinguishes IPC failures from R errors)
- Distinct process exit codes by category: 2 (transport), 3 (session), 4 (protocol)
- `R_NOT_AT_PROMPT` hint improved with actionable debugger exit instruction

Bootstraps the repo from scratch with a full-stack real-time prank disguised as a Kahoot join flow, targeting exactly 40 simultaneous mobile users.

## Architecture

- **`server.js`** — Express on port 3000, Socket.io for real-time events, 40-user hard cap via `Set`, rate-limited page routes (100 req/min)
- **`public/index.html`** — Mobile-first Kahoot purple join screen (nickname-only, no PIN), loading state → 10s countdown → full-screen red prank reveal

## Socket.io Event Flow

```
Player joins       → emit joinGame(nickname)     → server broadcasts userCountUpdate
Admin clicks START → emit startGame(adminSecret) → server broadcasts gameStarted
                                                 → client counts 10s → red prank screen
```

## Security

- Nickname sanitized server-side (strips `<>"'&`, enforced 20-char max) — client `maxlength` alone is bypassable
- `startGame` requires an `ADMIN_SECRET` token (env-configurable, default `kahoot-admin-2026`); unauthorized emits are silently dropped
- Rate limiting via `express-rate-limit` on both page routes

Bootstrap a greenfield React SPA for JoinU, a campus club intelligent-matching platform. The repo previously contained only a `README.md`.

## Stack
- React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + TailwindCSS v4 (`@tailwindcss/vite`) + React Router v6
- Zero UI icon libraries — emoji used throughout
- `vercel.json` SPA rewrites included

## Pages (10 routes)
| Route | Page |
|---|---|
| `/` | Identity selector — 新生 / 社团管理者 |
| `/student/login` | Student login with one-click demo entry |
| `/admin/login` | Admin login with one-click demo entry |
| `/student/home` | Hero search + category filter + club card list + bottom nav |
| `/student/assessment` | 8-question stepped quiz with animated progress bar |
| `/student/recommendations` | Profile card + Top-5 clubs with match % scores |
| `/student/club/:id` | Club detail — cover image, stats, activities, apply CTA |
| `/student/apply/:clubId` | Application form with bounce-animation success screen |
| `/student/applications` | Mock application status list (待审核/已通过/已拒绝) |
| `/admin/dashboard` | Stats cards + applicant table with profile tags |

## Data & Matching (`src/data.ts`, `src/matching.ts`)
- 12 mock clubs with full metadata: tags, activities, `matchKeywords`, `beginnerFriendly` rating, cover images via `picsum.photos`
- AI matching: assessment answers accumulate keyword votes → mapped to one of 6 profile types (创意表达型 / 技术探索型 / 社交活力型 / 公益服务型 / 学术研究型 / 运动健将型) → scored against club `matchKeywords` with beginner-friendly and recruiting-status bonuses

## Design
- Primary: `#F97316` (orange-500), background `#FFF8F5`, `rounded-2xl shadow-sm` cards, `bg-orange-50 text-orange-500 rounded-full` tags
- Mobile-first: `max-w-md mx-auto` throughout

author: aafre
body:
## Summary

Every prerendered page served to Googlebot has **duplicate meta tags**: the original hardcoded generic tags from `index.html` appear FIRST in `<head>`, followed by page-specific tags injected by react-helmet-async (`data-rh="true"`). Google reads the first `<meta name="description">` it encounters — the generic "EasyFreeResume is a 100% free resume builder" — on ALL pages. This explains 144K impressions with near-zero CTR on non-branded queries.

**Evidence (verified on production 2026-03-29):**
```
GET /blog/claude-resume-prompts (Googlebot UA)

Line 19: <meta name="description" content="EasyFreeResume is a 100% free resume builder...">      ← GENERIC (1st)
Line 74: <meta name="description" content="Best Claude prompts for resume writing..." data-rh>    ← CORRECT (2nd, ignored)
Line 74: <link rel="canonical" href="http://localhost:4173/blog/claude-resume-prompts" data-rh>    ← LOCALHOST BUG
```

Same pattern on every prerendered page (keyword pages, comparison pages, landing pages).

## Changes

- **`BlogLayout.tsx`** — Fix canonical URL: use hardcoded `BASE_URL` instead of `window.location.origin` (which resolves to `http://localhost:4173` during build-time prerendering). Also fixes `mainEntityOfPage.@id` in BlogPosting JSON-LD.

- **`prerender.ts`** — Add `cleanPrerenderedHtml()` post-processing that strips duplicate non-`data-rh` meta tags from prerendered HTML. **Safety rule**: only removes a generic tag when a `data-rh="true"` replacement exists — if Helmet didn't inject a page-specific tag, the generic fallback is preserved. Also replaces any remaining localhost URLs with production origin.

- **`app.py`** — Add Twitterbot, LinkedInBot, WhatsApp, TelegramBot, Slackbot to bot user-agent detection so social sharing previews get prerendered HTML with correct OG tags.

## Test plan

- [x] Run `cd resume-builder-ui && npm run build:prerender` locally
- [ ] Inspect `dist/prerendered/blog/claude-resume-prompts/index.html` — should have only ONE `<meta name="description">` with page-specific content, no generic "100% free resume builder"
- [ ] Inspect canonical URL — should be `https://easyfreeresume.com/...`, not `localhost`
- [ ] Spot-check: `/resume-keywords/customer-service`, `/easyfreeresume-vs-zety`, homepage
- [ ] After deploy: `curl -A Googlebot https://easyfreeresume.com/blog/claude-resume-prompts | grep description` — verify only page-specific description appears
- [ ] After deploy: `curl -A Twitterbot https://easyfreeresume.com/blog/claude-resume-prompts | grep og:title` — verify social bots get prerendered HTML

body:
## What does this PR do?

This PR introduces a robust mechanism to resolve menu bar icons without relying primarily on Screen Capture APIs. It accomplishes this by reading and extracting icons directly from app bundles (asset catalogs) and mapping system items to standard SF Symbols. This ensures icons are visible even when screen recording permissions are not granted. Additionally, it refactors the image cache for better thread safety and performance.

## PR Type

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] CI/CD related changes
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, renaming)
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Feature
- [ ] i18n/l10n (Translation/Localization)
- [x] Refactor
- [x] Performance improvement
- [ ] Test addition or update
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

If yes, please describe the impact and migration path:

## What is the current behavior?

The application relies heavily on the macOS Screen Capture APIs to render menu bar icons. If Screen Recording permissions are denied or if the capture fails transiently, icons appear blank or missing. Additionally, `MenuBarItemImageCache` had potential data-race vulnerabilities around the tracking of failed captures.
Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

- **Asset Catalog Parsing**: Added `AssetCatalogReader` to directly extract, evaluate, and score the best matching icons from third-party app bundles (`Assets.car` and raw layout resources).
- **SF Symbols Integration**: Added `MenuBarIconProvider` to reliably map known system menu bar items (e.g., WiFi, Bluetooth, Battery) to their corresponding dynamic SF Symbols.
- **Cache Thread Safety & Performance**: Added `failedCapturesLock` (`NSLock`) in `MenuBarItemImageCache` to make dictionary accesses thread-safe. Optimized memory allocations by using `.reserveCapacity()` where appropriate.
- **Improved Fallback Logic**: The system now prioritizing asset catalog/SF Symbol resolution *before* layering screen captures over them, immediately improving the initial visual state before permissions are granted.

## PR Checklist

- [x] I’ve built and run the app locally
- [x] I’ve checked for console errors or crashes
- [ ] I've run relevant tests and they pass
- [ ] I've added or updated tests (if applicable)
- [ ] I've updated documentation as needed
- [ ] I've verified localized strings work correctly (if i18n/l10n changes)

## Other information

This is a significant improvement for the onboarding experience, as users will now see recognizable icons immediately before having to grant any broad OS-level permissions like Screen Recording. 

### Notes for reviewers

- Please review the heuristic scoring logic in `AssetCatalogReader` (specifically the regex weighting, size penalties, and keyword bonuses) to see if the weighting makes sense.
- Verify the thread-safety locks introduced around the `failedCaptures` dictionary in `MenuBarItemImageCache`.

body:
## Summary

- **Move `import re` to module level** in `buildkite_step.py`: The `import re` was inside a for loop within `_prepare_commands()`, causing a redundant import on every iteration. Moved to the top of the file with the other imports.
- **Remove debug print statement**: Removed leftover `print(variables_to_inject)` from `convert_group_step_to_buildkite_step()`.
- **Fix inconsistent `DeviceType.value` comparisons**: Removed unnecessary `.value` accesses in `_get_step_plugin()` and `get_k8s_plugin()`. Since `DeviceType` extends `str`, direct enum comparison works correctly. Also switched from list to tuple for membership checks.
- **Remove dead code in `_create_block_step()`**: Removed unused `list_file_diff` parameter and a no-op `if` block that re-set `depends_on` to its already-initialized value of `[]`.
- **Remove dead code in AMD block step creation**: Removed `amd_block_step = None` immediately followed by reassignment, and removed an always-true `if amd_block_step:` guard.
- **Reduce K8s plugin template duplication**: Replaced three nearly identical template dicts (`h100_plugin_template`, `nebius_h200_plugin_template`, `a100_plugin_template`) with shared constants (`_COMMON_ENV`, `_COMMON_VOLUME_MOUNTS`, `_COMMON_VOLUMES`) and a `_build_k8s_template()` builder function. Also added a proper `ValueError` for unsupported device types instead of silently returning `None` and crashing.
- **Reduce Docker plugin template duplication**: Replaced three nearly identical template dicts (`docker_plugin_template`, `h200_plugin_template`, `b200_plugin_template`) with shared constants (`_COMMON_FIELDS`, `_COMMON_ENV`, `_DEVICE_CONFIGS`, `_DEFAULT_CONFIG`) and a single `get_docker_plugin()` implementation that constructs the plugin from config.

This introduces full Gamepad support for Marbles 3D.

author: raptor4mc
body:
### Motivation

- Provide a repo-bundled fallback JS loader for the web UI when compiled C++/WASM artifacts are not present to improve developer experience. 
- Make the web playground detect available web artifacts via a manifest so it can prefer real compiled artifacts and reject stub/fallback loaders.

### Description

- Add a fallback loader `web/magphos_wasm.js` that exposes minimal `Module.compileMagPhos`, `Module.analyzeMagPhos`, and sets `Module.__magphosFallback = true` to mark it as a non-compiled fallback. 
- Update `web/magphos_wasm_singlefile.js` to set `__magphosFallback = true` for parity with the new fallback loader. 
- Add a JSON manifest `web/magphos_artifacts.json` (and generate it in `tools/scripts/build_web.sh`) listing available `loaders` and `wasm` artifacts so the playground can discover artifacts at runtime. 
- Update `tools/scripts/build_web.sh` to emit `web/magphos_artifacts.json` after a successful web build and print its size. 
- Update `.gitignore` to un-ignore `web/magphos_wasm.js` so the fallback can be part of the repo. 
- Modify `web/playground.js` to load the artifact manifest via `loadArtifactManifest()`, use it to build `loaderCandidates` and `wasmCandidates`, add `isFallbackLoaderModule()` to detect fallback-only modules, and reject fallback-only loaders when attempting to select a compiled WASM runtime. 

### Testing

- No automated tests were run as part of this change.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide an integrated customer support workflow (tickets, email notifications, auto-reply) and better forum moderation/appeals handling. 
- Allow users to save/delete media in Cloudinary from the UI and enable admins to manage support tickets and cookies securely. 
- Improve UX with refreshed admin pages, a richer public UI (preview protections, waveform mini-player, metadata automation), and rebrand/core messaging to "YTConv".

### Description
- Added server-side support ticket system and moderation: new in-memory `supportTickets` store plus endpoints `POST /api/contact`, `POST /api/forum/moderation-report`, `GET /api/ticket/:ticketId`, `GET /api/admin/tickets`, `GET /api/admin/stats`, and `PATCH /api/admin/tickets/:ticketId` with admin bearer check via `isAdminBearerValid`.
- Cloudinary helpers and management: `extractCloudinaryPublicIdFromUrl`, `POST /api/cloudinary/delete` endpoint (resource ownership check), and client upload helpers; history now keeps cloud-saved items and deletion triggers Cloudinary delete.
- Email and notification integration: `sendSupportEmail` wrapper (uses existing mail transport), server sends admin notification and auto-reply on ticket creation, and UI calls EmailJS as a secondary channel for immediate emails.
- Forum moderation improvements: bad-words tracking, per-user violation counts and auto-bans, appeal flow that notifies admins by email, and auto-report endpoint for moderated content.
- Client/UI changes: overhaul of `public-ui` assets including `admin-cookies.html` (revamped admin cookies manager), added `admin-dashboard.html`, `admin-tickets.html`, `ticket-status.html`, and major `index.html` updates (AI Navigator integration, ticket form wiring, preview protections disabling downloads/context menu, WaveSurfer waveform mini-player, smart metadata toggles, multi-server selector, cloud save flows, history cloud-only behavior, and many label/content updates to reflect YTConv branding).
- Misc: maintenance info fallback enhancements, localization/right-to-left-friendly prompts, several UX improvements (toasts, progress, and friendly error messages) and small security/UI hardening (disable download in preview and protect context menu).

### Testing
- No automated tests were added or modified in this change set.
- Existing automated test suites were not changed as part of this PR.

author: fbraza
body:
## Summary

- Adds **log2(size-factor normalized counts)** as a third transformation option alongside VST and rlog in the `bulk-rnaseq-counts-to-de-deseq2` skill
- Based on the approach used by [Burton et al. (2024, *Immunity*)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.immuni.2024.05.023) for tissue Treg RNA-seq PCA analysis ([GitHub](https://github.com/AdrianListon/TissueTregs))
- Includes a biologically motivated `filter_transcripts_per_cell()` function for FACS-sorted samples

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `scripts/log2_normalization.R` | **New** — `apply_log2_normalization()` (3 zero-handling modes) + `filter_transcripts_per_cell()` |
| `scripts/transformations.R` | `method="log2"` added to `transform_counts()` + updated guide |
| `references/decision-guide.md` | Option C (log2) with decision tree, trade-offs, and paper reference |
| `SKILL.md` | Decision 1 now lists all 3 transformation options |

### Why add this?

The standard DESeq2 pipeline recommends VST/rlog for visualization (PCA, heatmaps). However, some published analyses use `log2(normalized counts)` instead — a simpler approach that preserves absolute expression magnitude but offers no variance stabilization. When reproducing such analyses, users need this option.

**Key trade-offs vs VST/rlog:**
- Simpler and more interpretable
- Preserves absolute magnitude differences  
- No variance stabilization → high-expression genes dominate PCA
- Genes with zero counts in ANY sample are removed (can lose 50%+ of genes)

### Decision tree (updated)

```
Downstream task?
├─ Differential expression → raw counts with DESeq()
└─ PCA / clustering / heatmap →
    ├─ Standard (recommended): vst (n>30) or rlog (n≤30)
    └─ Log2 normalized: replicating published analyses,
       absolute scale PCA, or exclude zero-count genes
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `apply_log2_normalization()` works with all 3 zero_handling modes
- [ ] Verify `filter_transcripts_per_cell()` produces expected gene filtering
- [ ] Verify `transform_counts(dds, method = "log2")` integrates correctly
- [ ] Verify existing `method = "auto"`, `"vst"`, `"rlog"` still work unchanged
- [ ] Review decision-guide.md for clarity and correctness

body:
## Summary
- fix Extended live-order quantity/price serialization to respect venue increments
- add live order-state models, observers, storage wiring, and API endpoint for the latest execution
- add Paradex `orders-history` fallback when closed IOC orders disappear from direct order lookup

## Why
Live testing surfaced two real integration gaps:
1. Extended rejected a valid-looking ARB order with `Invalid quantity precision`; the preview/signer path was over-formatting decimals.
2. Paradex accepted an IOC order and later reported it as closed/unfilled, but `GET /v1/orders/{id}` eventually returned `ORDER_ID_NOT_FOUND`; the system needs a fallback to `orders-history` to classify closed IOC orders correctly.

## Live findings folded into this PR
- Extended precision fix was verified with a real live submit path.
- Paradex order-state fallback was verified live against the previous IOC order id and classified it as `unfilled` with `cancel_reason=REMAINING_IOC_CANCEL`.
- Extended is flat after the cleanup; no open Extended positions remain.

## Validation
- `uv run ruff check .`
- `uv run mypy $(find src apps packages tests -name '*.py' -type f)`
- `uv run pytest`

author: mahdihassani12
body:
### Motivation
- Province dropdowns and many filters relied on `check_access()` and were missing entries when saved access points used different separators (spaces vs underscores). 
- The inconsistency caused province visibility to fail across multiple pages that use province-based access checks. 
- The change preserves existing backward-compatibility behavior for users who have no `province_accessibility/*` entries.

### Description
- Updated `check_access()` in `lib/_configuration.php` to handle province name variants when `access_path` starts with `province_accessibility/`.
- Extracts the province portion from the access path and builds normalized variants (`original`, `space->underscore`, `underscore->space`) using `str_replace` and `array_unique`.
- Checks each variant against the lowercased `$_SESSION['holu_accessibilities']` and returns access if any variant is present.
- Keeps the existing fallback that grants full province access when no `province_accessibility/` entries exist in the stored accessibilities.

### Testing
- Ran `php -l lib/_configuration.php` and it reported no syntax errors.

author: gianoteo07-cloud
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a complete Nginx-based architecture for the existing Registro Elettronico project so the class can see theory + a working demo.
- Expose a single gateway that routes requests to role-specific Angular frontends, the Flask API and Keycloak, and demonstrate this configuration via Docker.
- Ensure frontends run as separate builds (docenti / studenti) and keep Keycloak/API verification working when behind a reverse proxy.

### Description
- Added an Nginx gateway configuration at `nginx/nginx.conf` that routes `/docenti/`, `/studenti/`, `/api/` and `/auth/` to the appropriate upstreams.
- Extended `compose.yml` to a full Docker stack including `mysql`, `keycloak`, `backend`, `frontend-docente`, `frontend-studente` and `nginx`, and mounted the nginx config into the container.
- Added Dockerfiles: `backend/Dockerfile` (Flask runtime) and `frontend/Dockerfile` (Angular build with `BASE_HREF` and `PORTAL_ROLE` build args and an Nginx static server), and a simple frontend Nginx conf at `frontend/docker/default.conf`.
- Updated frontend runtime config `frontend/public/app-config.js` to use relative paths (`/api`, `/auth`) and added `portalRole` support.
- Updated frontend code to support portal-specific behavior: `AuthService` (`getPortalRole`, redirect/redirect URI handling), `role.guard.ts` (block cross-portal access), and `HomeComponent` (dynamic title/subtitle per portal).
- Modified backend `backend/app.py` to accept `KEYCLOAK_JWKS_URL` and `KEYCLOAK_ISSUER` environment variables (keeps sensible defaults) so JWT verification works when Keycloak is proxied.
- Added lesson material and demo notes at `docs/lezione-nginx.md` and updated `README.md` with architecture and quick-start instructions.

### Testing
- Ran Python static checks by compiling backend modules with `python -m py_compile backend/app.py backend/DatabaseWrapper.py`, which completed successfully.
- Attempted to validate the Compose file with `docker compose config` but the environment has no `docker` binary, so the compose validation could not be executed (`/bin/bash: docker: command not found`).
- No containerized integration tests were executed in this environment due to the missing Docker runtime.

GlobalStats
 struct.

update_global_stats

db.rs
 called

author: daydaybeatz
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a palette-aware color helper and a small set of common gameplay utilities to simplify collision, distance, and table field manipulation in the Lua runtime and exported runtime.
- Make it possible to use palette slots where `color()`/draw state is expected and to offer convenient collision and value helpers for typical game objects (rectangles and circles).

### Description
- Added `pcolor(index)` to the editor runtime and export runtime to set the current draw color from `projectRef.palette` and return the palette value, and exposed it to Lua via `push('pcolor', ...)` so it can be called from scripts using `pcolor(1)`.
- Implemented new Lua helper functions in `LUA_RUNTIME_HELPERS`: `distance(a, b)`, `col(a, b)` (AABB rectangle overlap using `x,y,w,h`), `col2(a, b)` (circular overlap using `x,y` and `r`/`radius`), `mod_value(table, key, amount)`, `set_value(table, key, value)`, and `get_value(table, key)`.
- Updated the in-editor API documentation (`CODE_API_DOCS`) with entries for `pcolor`, `distance`, `col`, `col2`, `mod_value`, `set_value`, and `get_value` so they appear in the docs panel.
- Applied the changes across the main runtime, the exported runtime generator, and the Lua bind layer so runtime and exported builds behave consistently.

### Testing
- Searched and verified code additions with `rg` and `nl` to confirm new functions and docs were inserted (searches present in rollout transcript and returned expected hits). (succeeded)
- Ran `git -C /workspace/trycode-v2 diff --check` to ensure no whitespace/diff issues and `git status --short` to confirm changes staged; both returned clean results and a commit was created with the message `Add palette color and collision/value helper APIs`. (succeeded)

author: copilot
body:
The PDF viewer's fit-to-width scaling was silently broken on load (measuring a hidden element with `clientWidth === 0`), the zoom badge never reflected the computed scale, the canvas container had a flex layout bug causing height overflow, and the contents sidebar showed nothing useful for documents without an embedded PDF outline.

## Changes

### Scaling & fit-to-width
- **Fix auto-fit measurement**: Replace `wrap.clientWidth` (hidden at compute time, always `0`) with `$el('ws-pdf-view').clientWidth` — the always-visible flex parent
- **Zoom badge sync**: Update `ws-zoom-badge` immediately after computing the fitted scale on load
- **`wsFitWidth()`**: New exported helper that recomputes and applies fit-to-width scale at any time

### Dynamic resize
- **`_wsAttachResizeObserver()`**: Shared helper that wires a `ResizeObserver` on `ws-pdf-view`, RAF-debounced via `ws.resizeRaf`, disconnecting any prior observer. Called in both `books.js` and `userDocs.js` after PDF load — PDF now re-fits automatically when the drag splitter is moved or the window resizes.

### Layout
- Canvas wrap: `height:100%` → `flex:1;min-height:0` — correct way to fill a flex-column parent without overflow issues

### Contents panel
- **Outline fallback**: When no embedded PDF outline and no hard-coded outline exist, generates ~30 evenly-spaced page entries so the sidebar is never empty
- **User-doc outline**: Calls `_wsBuildOutline()` instead of rendering a static "Your document" placeholder — uploaded PDFs now get outline extraction (or the page-list fallback)

author: adev3141
body:
### Motivation

- Move from per-task Metriq API calls to a benchmark-native JSON feed to support richer benchmark-family evidence and platform indexing for readiness and risk signals.
- Improve UX by surfacing technical formulas and methodology as collapsible details to reduce visual noise while keeping full transparency.
- Publish and protect new benchmark-native global documents in Firestore to support the migrated data model and maintain backwards compatibility for legacy documents.

### Description

- Replaced Metriq per-task API integration with fetching `benchmark.latest.json` and a platforms index (`METRIQ_BENCHMARK_LATEST_URL` and `METRIQ_PLATFORMS_INDEX_URL`) and added `fetchBenchmarkRows` and `fetchPlatformsIndex` helpers. 
- Introduced a benchmark-oriented selection pipeline: new types (`MetriqBenchmarkRow`, `BenchmarkSignalCandidate`), new selection functions (`selectBestBenchmarkResult`, `selectPhysicalQubitsCandidate`, `isBenchmarkFamilyAllowed`, `adjustMetricValueForTask`, `matchesRelaxedTaskMetric`) and synthesized/fallback AQ logic (`synthesizeAqSignalFromCoverage`, `deriveAqSignalForMetrics`) to produce frontier signals when direct AQ is absent. 
- Updated metric normalization/aggregation and global doc construction to use the effective AQ proxy when necessary, changed `source_url` and source labeling to the benchmark feed, and tightened stale windows and scheduling (`METRICS_STALE_AFTER_HOURS` and `syncMetriqMetrics` schedule). 
- Hardened HTTP fetches with a 25s timeout, combined abort signals, and jittered retry backoff in `fetchJson`, and added `BENCHMARK_FAMILY_BY_TASK` to gate accepted benchmark families per task. 
- UI changes in `app/page.tsx` add a reusable `CollapsibleTechnicalDetails` component, convert multiple methodology/notes blocks into collapsible sections, and adjust several labels/descriptions for readiness/threat/benchmark evidence. 
- Firestore rules extended to expose new benchmark-native public collections and corresponding history collections (e.g., `/global/benchmark_frontier`, `/global/readiness_projection`, `/global/threat_signals`, and history variants) while keeping legacy `metriq_*` documents readable for compatibility.

### Testing

- Type-check and production build (`npm run build`) executed in CI and completed successfully. 
- Unit tests and integration tests (`npm test`) covering ingestion and normalization logic ran and passed. 
- Firestore rules validation / lint step (`firebase rules:lint` or equivalent CI rule checks) executed and returned no blocking errors.

### Motivation
- Strips should be visually simpler by removing the trailing "Last:" line, and controllers need a quick way to command an ILS intercept via the heading UI so the simulated pilot will intercept the localizer and provide the requested readback.

### Description
- Removed the strip footer readout block from `StripCard` to hide the `Last: ...` instruction text (file: `UKRadarSim/ContentView.swift`).
- Added an `ILS` toggle/button to the heading picker and threaded an `ilsModeArmed` state through `HeadingPicker`/`StripCard`/`StripBayColumn`/`MainRadarView` so the next `Send` will treat the heading as an ILS interception request (files: `UKRadarSim/ContentView.swift`, `UKRadarSim/MainRadarView.swift`).
- Introduced a new instruction type `ilsClearance` and `armILSIntercept(stripID:)` in `SimulationEngine` which sets `approachType = "ILS"`, marks the strip as cleared and enables auto-landing behavior (file: `UKRadarSim/SimulationEngine.swift`).
- Updated phrase generation in `VoiceReadbackService` so an ILS-armed heading issues the readback style `head XXX` and appends `cleared ILS approach` to the assembled instruction segments (file: `UKRadarSim/VoiceReadbackService.swift`).

### Testing
- Attempted to run a project build with `xcodebuild -project UKRadarSim.xcodeproj -scheme UKRadarSim -sdk iphonesimulator -configuration Debug build`, but it failed in this environment because `xcodebuild` is not available (`xcodebuild: command not found`).
- No automated unit tests were present or executed as part of this change, and runtime behavior (speech/readback and ILS auto-capture) was not validated by a build in this environment.

`$DOTFILES` is an absolute path, so prepending `./` produced invalid double-slash paths (e.g. `.//Users/you/.dotfiles/scripts/update.sh`), causing `zsh: no such file or directory` on every `update` or `bootstrap` invocation.

```zsh
# Before
alias update="./$DOTFILES/scripts/update.sh"
alias bootstrap="./$DOTFILES/scripts/bootstrap.sh"

# After
alias update="$DOTFILES/scripts/update.sh"
alias bootstrap="$DOTFILES/scripts/bootstrap.sh"
```

body:
AVRoutePickerView manages AirPlay routing for AVPlayer/AVKit sessions, which is a completely separate layer from AVAudioEngine (CoreAudio system default output). Selecting a device in one did not update the other, so they appeared to fight — selecting Linn Selekt in System Settings deselected it in the route picker and vice versa.

AudioOutputPickerView replaces it: a button that opens a native NSMenu listing every CoreAudio output device (with a checkmark on the current default). Selecting an item calls AudioObjectSetPropertyData to update kAudioHardwarePropertyDefaultOutputDevice — the same property that System Settings writes. AVAudioEngine follows that property automatically, so the picker, the engine, and System Settings all stay in sync.

author: ariessa
body:
## Problem

Each ERC-8183 job can only attach one hook. Jobs needing multiple concerns (escrow, privacy, reputation) must cram everything into a single monolithic contract -- hard to build, hard to audit, impossible to reuse.

Additionally, BaseACPHook's setBudget selector still used the old 3-param signature `setBudget(uint256,uint256,bytes)` while AgenticCommerce expects `setBudget(uint256,address,uint256,bytes)`. This meant `_preSetBudget` and `_postSetBudget` callbacks silently never fired.

> Note: All instances of ACP that originated from this repository are now renamed to ERC8183.

## Solution

- Add MultiHookRouter -- implements IACPHook, fans out beforeAction/afterAction to per-selector ordered sub-hook lists per job. No core contract changes needed.
- Per-selector architecture: each hookable function (setBudget, fund, submit, complete, reject) has its own hook array per job, so hooks only fire for the selectors they're configured on
- Per-hook data dispatch: optParams encoded as abi.encode(bytes[]) splits data per sub-hook; empty optParams broadcasts to all 
- IERC8183HookMetadata interface for selector completeness validation -- hooks declare cross-selector dependencies, router enforces at fund time and in batchConfigureHooks
- De-whitelisted hook resilience: sub-hooks removed from core whitelist after configuration are skipped with an event instead of reverting
- Fix BaseACPHook setBudget selector, abi.decode, and virtual signatures to include the token parameter
- Update FundTransferHook and BiddingHook _preSetBudget overrides to match
- Rename acp -> erc8183: BaseACPHook to BaseERC8183Hook, acpContract to erc8183Contract, onlyACP to onlyERC8183, @acp/ remapping to @erc8183/
- Update acp submodule to latest (evaluation grace period, expired open jobs)
- Add documentation with architecture overview, per-selector config, data dispatch, and flow diagrams

## Audit
The MultiHookRouter contract has been audited. No critical or high severity findings were identified.

author: adrianschmidt-bot
body:
## Problem

The **Gather Pieces** feature places pieces too close together when pieces have tabs (the curvy jigsaw connectors). Tabs overlap between adjacent groups.

The root cause is in `getGroupVisualBounds()` — it only used `edge.start` and `edge.end` points (corner vertices) to compute bounding boxes, ignoring tab geometry that extends beyond those points via SVG path curves.

## Solution

Added a `getPathBounds()` helper that parses SVG path commands and includes all control points and endpoints from bezier curves (`C`, `c`, `Q`, `q`, `S`, `s`, etc.) in the bounding box calculation. This produces a conservative (slightly larger) but guaranteed bounding box that prevents tab overlap.

Updated `getGroupVisualBounds()` to use path bounds in addition to edge start/end points.

## Tests

- 12 new tests for `getPathBounds()` covering all SVG path command types
- 1 new integration test verifying tab geometry affects layout spacing
- All 692 existing tests continue to pass

Fixes #192

author: fdcastel
body:
## Motivation

When using `YamlDerivedType(Type)` or `YamlDerivedTypeAttribute(Type)` with only a `Tag` (no discriminator), the constructor doc comment stated the entry would be "the default when no discriminator matches." This was misleading — the actual behavior correctly treats tag-only entries as tag dispatch participants only, not as the default derived type.

### Scenario

```csharp
DerivedTypeMappings =
{
    [typeof(PullMonitorConfiguration)] =
    [
        new YamlDerivedType(typeof(CheckInMonitorConfiguration)) { Tag = \"!checkin\" },
        new YamlDerivedType(typeof(DnsMonitorConfiguration)) { Tag = \"!dns\" },
    ]
}
```

With this configuration, an untagged YAML mapping should deserialize as the base type `PullMonitorConfiguration`, not as `CheckInMonitorConfiguration`.

## Changes

1. **Clarified doc comments** on both `YamlDerivedType(Type)` and `YamlDerivedTypeAttribute(Type)` constructors to explicitly document that:
   - Default is set only when **both** `Discriminator` and `Tag` are `null`
   - When `Tag` is set, the entry participates in tag-based dispatch only

2. **Added 10 comprehensive tests** covering:
   - Attribute-based tag-only entries: untagged values deserialize as base type
   - Runtime tag-only entries (`DerivedTypeMappings`): untagged values deserialize as base type
   - Dictionary with mixed tagged and untagged values
   - Explicit default type coexisting with tag-only entries
   - Roundtrip serialization for both attribute and runtime paths
